Peter, A few weeks ago, I told you we started the general election on empty — that we spent everything we had to win the primary. Here's what I didn't make clear: the other side never stopped raising money. Valadao didn't have a competitive primary and is sitting on nearly _$3 million_ thanks to corporate PACs and special interests who write checks year-round, election or not. We don't have that kind of money machine. We built ours one grassroots donor at a time. And we have to rebuild it again now that we are in the general election. **The fact is, we're at a disadvantage.** I know it's tempting to think that's just how things work, that money always wins. You’ll never convince me of that, but we have to be willing to fight for it. Which is why I need to ask: **[Tonight marks our mid-July fundraising deadline and we're not yet halfway to our goal for the month. I need your help closing that gap. I’m sitting here alone staring at our latest reports, and I’m struggling. I usually try to stay strong for the team, but looking at these numbers...**_I’m_**** __distraught__**** _._**
The truth is, we are much further behind than I ever imagined. It’s a weight I can’t carry alone anymore. I fear that we’re letting you down and failing our mission.
I’ve spent the last few days trying to find a way out, and I’ve finally reached the point where I have to humble myself and ask for help. **_[I’ve poured the full truth into a private note for you here:](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)_**

I wouldn't ask if it wasn't urgent, but time is ticking. I hope you'll understand.
Best, Katie

name: Melat Kiros
subject: Denver was not an isolated victory.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Justice Democrats
body:
This movement’s next fight is in MI-13
#
I want to tell you about my friend Donavan McKinney.
A few weeks before our election, Donavan came to Denver and stood beside us while millions in dark money poured into our district in an effort to crush our campaign and silence us.
**Yesterday, I was in Michigan rallying with Donavan and fellow Justice Democrat Chris Rabb, because that same political machine that tried to stop us has picked Donavan as its next target.**
Donavan is running for Congress in Michigan’s 13th District, one of the most underserved districts in America and a place built by working people who clock in shift after shift while billionaires, corporations, and career politicians get richer off their labor.
He knows that struggle because he lived it too, and now he serves in the Michigan House, fighting for workers, families, and communities that Washington has abandoned for decades.
_And that is exactly why the establishment is terrified of him._
His multimillionaire opponent has been propped up by AIPAC and the same network of billionaire donors, corporate interests, and dark money PACs that spent millions trying to defeat us. They are flooding this race with money and attacks because they know what happens when working people elect someone who cannot be bought.
**These groups know Denver was not an isolated victory, that Donavan can win, and that if we keep winning races like this, their grip on the Democratic Party starts to break.**
**[So if you can, I’m asking you to come through for Donavan the way you came through for me by splitting a contribution between his campaign and Justice Democrats today.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260715-2-dm.cf9Tdj&refcode=em20260715-38033&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=38033%2E1203867%2E3-EEke)**
**[Contribute $10](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260715-2-dm.cf9Tdj&refcode=em20260715-38033&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=21&akid=38033%2E1203867%2E3-EEke)**
Donavan showed up for us when powerful forces were trying to erase our movement. Now they are betting that the rest of us will look away while they do the same thing to him.
_We cannot let them win that bet._
From Denver to Detroit, we are building a movement that refuses to settle for corporate Democrats who serve billionaires while working families fall further behind.
**[I’m standing with Donavan in Michigan, but we need you standing with us, too.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260715-2-dm.cf9Tdj&refcode=em20260715-38033&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=38033%2E1203867%2E3-EEke)**
— Melat

name: James Carville
subject: Democrats have needed this for a long time.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Folks, it’s James Carville.
I’ve spent nearly half a century helping Democrats win elections, and I’m gonna tell you something plainly:
For too long, we have waited until the house was already on fire before deciding to buy a hose.
We wait until a race becomes a crisis.
We wait until a great candidate is getting buried in attack ads.
We wait until Republicans have already built the infrastructure, raised the money, and defined the battlefield.
Then everybody starts running around asking what happened.
Well, Raja Krishnamoorthi has gone and done something about it.
He founded Equal Opportunity Now [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email] to find and support bold leaders and important causes before it’s too late — leaders who will stand up to Donald Trump and the MAGA movement, fight for working families, and actually deliver results.
And all I can say is:
FINALLY.
Finally, an organization that understands we cannot defeat MAGA with timid candidates, stale talking points, and a last-minute panic.
But Raja cannot build this by himself.
Will you contribute $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Equal Opportunity Now find, fund, and support the leaders Democrats need to start winning again? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
SUPPORT EQUAL OPPORTUNITY NOW! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Now, I know Raja.
He is smart. He is tough. And he knows firsthand what opportunity can mean.
His family came to this country with very little. They relied on public housing and food stamps. He worked his way from Peoria all the way to Congress.
And instead of pulling the ladder up behind him, Raja has spent his career fighting to make sure the next family gets the same shot.
That means standing up for workers.
Holding powerful corporations and corrupt politicians accountable.
Defending immigrants, voting rights, and every American targeted by Trump’s politics of division.
And now he is putting that experience toward building the next generation of Democratic leadership.
Here’s the truth: The leaders we need are already out there.
They are running for city council, state legislature, Congress, and offices most national donors are not paying attention to yet.
They have the courage.
They have the ideas.
What they do not always have is the money, infrastructure, and early support necessary to compete.
That is where Equal Opportunity Now comes in.
Please chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Raja build the organization Democrats should have built years ago. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
HELP DEMOCRATS WIN: DONATE TODAY! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
We’ve got a good battle plan, now, let’s help Raja build this damn thing.
-- James Carville
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

**_Mike’s original email:_**
Peter, the affordability crisis in this country is spiraling out of control. Families are struggling to afford healthcare, housing, gas, groceries and other basic necessities. That’s why I introduced the American Affordability Act to help put money back into Americans’ pockets across the board.

My legislation lowers costs for housing, energy, healthcare, childcare and education costs through a series of commonsense tax credits and deductions.

**_[Add your name now to support my efforts to lower costs. Your signature adds urgency to my message that we need concrete solutions to fix the affordability crisis in our country. **[SUPPORT LOWER COSTS](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135345346/633967638/868073187?source=EM_NBI_MT_20260715_PT_AffordabilityBill_0_3MO_TeamThompson_NA_NA_NA-2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NDQ0OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmYjYwOTliYS1iMjgwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=IwnjopK5o7-DK30e03AGiOeLGgdUDgbpQBBnzNZyvp8=&emci=de6099ba-b280-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=fb6099ba-b280-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=2678920)**
Gas, food, and rent prices across the country are hitting unprecedented levels. We need to do everything we can to make progress towards affordability.

But I’m not looking to make a quick fix. I want to build long-term economic security for families through my American Affordability Act. It will give tax credits to make housing more affordable, assist with childcare and adoption expenses, help lower monthly healthcare costs, and even expand tax credits for education.

Everyone will benefit from the American Affordability Act. **It’s about time we all come together to start fighting for the American people.**

This is just the first step, Peter. There are just 20 days left until our August 4 primary election, Peter.

Our primary isn't the finish line—**it's the first step.** I could give you a hundred reasons as to why we need to turn out strong. Instead, I'll give you just one: _America can't afford to wait any longer for new leadership in the House._

After August 4th, we will turn our full attention to the fight ahead in November. **But it all starts by building the strongest campaign we can over these next 20 days.**

Every day, families are paying more for necessities like groceries and gas than they should. Every day, our rights and freedoms face new attacks. Every day, we see Republican politicians in Washington, DC choosing partisan politics over solving the problems people actually face. Every day we witness more grift and corruption from the Trump administration without as much as a raised eyebrow from the Republican majority. And the sooner we win our primary, _the sooner we can get to work holding this seat and flipping the House in November._

I left my pediatrics practice in 2018 and ran for Congress under circumstances similar to those we face right now: Donald Trump unrestrained by his party. But things are even worse now. He's not just reckless; he's vengeful. He's surrounded by loyalists and sycophants, emboldened in his second term, and unafraid to abuse power. He's also working hard to tip the scales in the upcoming midterm election.

But it is hard to sow doubt about an election with overwhelming turnout and a decisive Democratic victory. That's why, over the next 20 days, our campaign will be working nonstop to reach voters across WA-08. name: Dan Cox
subject: Wes Moore's PJM Price Cap Offers No Relief To Marylanders
body:
, Today, Wes Moore announced he is extending price caps on PJM, but this is no solution or help to Maryland's energy crisis. | |
---
| | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:

WES MOORE’S PJM COST CAP EXTENSION OFFERS NO RELIEF OR SOLUTION TO MARYLAND’S ENERGY CRISIS**

Frederick, MD – July 15, 2026

Governor Wes Moore is celebrating an agreement that extends electricity price cap rates through 2030 as though it is a victory for Maryland families. It is not. _**This extension is a political cover-up, not energy relief.**_ Maryland families are still being forced to pay electric bills of _**$600, $800, and even over $1,200 a month.**_ Wes Moore touts his $12.50 per month in average savings; however, while those same caps remain in place, BGE has already requested another average $8-per-month increase from state regulators. _**Marylanders don’t need a political spin.**_ They need lower electric rates through more reliable, affordable power generation--not temporary caps that leave today’s unaffordable bills largely unchanged. Families and businesses are experiencing growing concerns over grid reliability, an inadequate supply of electricity to meet increasing demand, and an energy policy that leaves our state less prepared for future growth. Maryland deserves an abundant, reliable, and affordable energy supply. Instead, **_Wes Moore implements policies that normalize high prices._** Governor Moore's plan manages the symptoms while leaving the underlying problem untouched.

A Dan Cox administration will take a different approach. Instead of capping already outrageous costs, we will work to reverse them. We will pursue policies that increase Maryland's electricity supply, restore dependable generation where feasible, and expand access to affordable, reliable, and responsible energy. More available power means greater reliability, increased competition, and lower costs for Maryland families and businesses.

Marylanders should not have to structure their household budgets around overwhelming electric bills. Those hard-earned dollars should be available for buying a home, saving for retirement, taking a family vacation, investing in a child's education, or building a stronger financial future.

**_Maryland can once again be a state where affordable, dependable energy fuels economic growth instead of draining family budgets. That is the difference between managing a crisis and solving one._**

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1941, New York Yankees center fielder Joe DiMaggio [recorded a hit in his 56th consecutive game](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DtuwzAQBNDTUJ2F5cckXbBwkLhzmhRBKoESl9YmtGRQawu-faBcId1gBnjFfJ67c6RC0-U9XjFwnrsJ16UgM9YtUo3TwpV-cIn1ghPTFHvsFCi7A7eTtkuRyrMzTQoZUaFuMEjnjTxY46AZAxh03qucc0p7cHmIWiaMB4DeobOmobBp4KSVAM74Nu1134Me7EFL9IMXBjARz7X9nmniEXN5zg-s7TBfmxJG5tsi9FGok1CndV3b53zne4_bvjWRh1Ho00Po15e3WgZpvz78sakh3VYqhRbrhIHLNVL5I_lfPzyC-g0AAP__e6FxRA), still the longest hitting streak in baseball history. The streak ended the next day in Cleveland, and many still consider this record to be unbreakable. So, is it hot enough for you where you live? The ongoing heat wave and heavy rain blasting much of America got us thinking about extreme weather events, and which type was worst. Of course, everyone at _The Flyover_ had a different opinion. Let us know what you think in today's _Poll_ , and you can reply directly to this email if you want to explain further. For nearly 30 years, almost every major Alzheimer's drug has chased the same sticky protein in the brain, and families have been handed the same modest results over and over. This week, researchers went after something else entirely, and what they found has the whole field tuning in. It could be the biggest shift in how this disease is treated in a generation, and it all comes down to a shot given just twice a year. In today's episode of _The Flyover Podcast_ , Ayla breaks down what researchers found and what still has to be proven before this reaches anyone. Nineteen states have already passed laws to lock their clocks on permanent daylight saving time, while more than a dozen others have introduced bills going the opposite direction, toward permanent standard time. The bill now heads to the Senate, where its path is far from certain. Sen. # AMERICA FIRST. NAVY VETERAN. PROVEN LEADER.
---
---
| Dear Peter,
I'm Heather Moraitis, George's wife, and I want to share my family's story with you. George voted to support families when he served in the FL House of Representatives. Nameless organizations are spreading lies about his position and they are twisting a story of faith, family, and freedom.
But here is the truth. George is not afraid to stand for what is right. He was also recently endorsed by Florida Family Action for his commitment to supporting strong families in Florida.
Yes, George was the only person to vote in the FL House for 16 and 17 year-olds to get married with the following conditions: a pregnancy was involved, they had parental support, and they had the consent of a judge. He voted to keep the law the same. The same way it was when my mom and dad got married at 16 in 1971 in Fort Lauderdale.
The legislature changed the marriage age in FL to 18 when George was in the FL House. George was the only vote supporting young people like my parents, who choose life, and choose to raise their child with a married mom and a dad.
My mom was my hero and she passed away a few years ago, after fighting dementia. When she knew she was dying, she asked me to tell her story one day. That day is here.
Her story is a beautiful story of trusting in God and living an abundant life filled with deep love. She loved others deeply and she was deeply loved by others.
I interviewed my mom, so I could capture her story. She wanted everyone to know that choosing life at 15, and marrying my dad at 16, was the best decision she made. They went on to have my brothers and always said we were the best gifts from God. But don't take my words. Spend a few minutes with my mom and hear her story. I hope you will have a better understanding of why George voted for my mom. George will always fight for freedom, for families, and for Florida!
---
---

## Tornado Hits San Antonio Amid Flooding
A tornado [touched down Wednesday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u6zAMBeCnsTcb1M-17EHDXbKla0eDCelYqCIFEhs7b1-4yBt0JYhz8J3P83zGEEO6feCdvexLnhNvNbIIl1lySUh5DVIrJkySU8gxpK9Zgx46cJ0aZsIQX7NtyV-AJtWyV260apocmHb1ejSEDsBY46xVVx70aP9No0PlFkRogz_CwKlBKVAWeiLUQIYWuhq0F9NYYAqSSy8rC-9Yl_jKTy79Nd_b6FeRR23M_0afGn3atq1f8q6HNX9Xyel4Os6MsnJp9OmN6g5VVzF1b1dbPD22EGOog2ss3O4Y4m-F_G2Yp9c_AQAA___9onle) near The Rim in northwest Bexar County, [damaging an apartment complex](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ_GdF7ZYy4sBUUadzdtSmQ8w8W6Xs_KnsDu20dEeYPU5-j8fL8-l8-QcipfP8ODZnltvBQ6WyYRqotwLQF5T9JaKKEIl8Q5le8FDAzajNoOC4aU30vf4bwanGxHsx3vvZ2m0bhunx18rOCm7W4MGMLNuLuL0zpgtNuIuHZpvsLMaAdrje3NDTGAQYcbRhf61aneECbhepOdhF6hbfnNB9Vb5EeX513k2ZT7ocAr8Od53r5bkEtU4K83CnzmGLICf1Up8GZU4O2HAn9ZdeRSKIo-Ep1Um257qKSfOws3fSQkbpo3_Q-HTkUXrrKf1ESv9ApVR_5d5K3Ad3XG55lyTm0YVW--HiHlv0Pl__AeM_wJAAD__-qdkVk) and businesses as slow-moving storms continued to drench South Texas and the Hill Country. The heaviest rain, up to 16 inches, has fallen in Uvalde County, where officials reported [25 high-water rescues](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkEHSoyAQRk-DOyxAxLhgMRt3_2xnaXXsjlIhYEGPJrefSio3mAu873vvz8_8AyGGtP6GB3l-3vKc6KyRmKnMnEsCzFvgWiFB4pxCjiHdZ6OMk2qQ2s0IIb5m26C_Khx1Q14PF6vHcVBds3nXLco6ZyxaBNPb3ikYLpfriNQ7tSxN8G-YGrTTWmmrWkQwCju84dKBvXbCKsLAubS8EdMT6i2-8kGlXfKjiX5j3qvofgkzCTOd59ne11RbPoSZ3mhhJjUIM-lemGkjOF6yQEhV3ol2iYXSsoW0ypr_8iY_A_JrLgvtuTChrJDkN4AwU1M87meIMVQ3CKvWB4T4ucP_F_Hw5l8AAAD__xinh34) by Wednesday morning. A Flash Flood Emergency was later declared for Boerne, where [crews pulled residents](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDHOozAQRk9jOpBtHIwLF9vQZdst0YCHMIpjI3s2JLdfsVf4y09P-p70_tznO1Ck9PgNL_T82fKc8KwRmbHMnEuCkHfiWiFB4pwoR0rPWUs9tNK2apgDUPzOpgl-kcGpBr2yo1HOWdk3u18W48AuPerb5py6mdWOEqTdRjWOo1MN-etMWjUoJZWRXQigZejDFtYezNILIzEQ59LxjowfqFv85jeWbs2vJvqd-aii_yX0JPR0nmf3rMAXvCYC71iEni6L0JO0Qk_qdiFgLG3Buv7F2u5wHJgoPVpK7ZKxJBR6aooPx0kxUh2sMPLxAor_vfyzWm-v_wUAAP__6y9-Dg) from rising water near Main Street. No deaths or injuries have been reported. Governor Greg Abbott [issued disaster declarations](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u2zAQhE9DdTT4I4tRwSKNupc2pbDSLi3CNCmQa-s5pw_kK7xqigHmm5m_X_MXxBTz7Q88yPN3KHOmoyVipjpzqRmwbJFbgwyZS44lxXyfjTKDVE7qYUaI6T33HfpF4ag78tr96vU4OmW7zbvRLFcLIcC4kF2dIrWofsRgsSc7XLvozzDl9KC10r26IIJRaDHgaqFfrOgVYeRSL7wR0ze0kN7lRfWylkeX_Ma8N2F_CzMJMx3Hcbk34NMUZjrXnAIcS4YkzHTShJmUE2bSV2GmjeD1lhVibvJOtEuslNct5pts5cmb_DAlBKYqsRx5L8_aZCKUXCSWf5SbLEFWauuTTlpXPe5HTCm2wYle3R4Q06ct_-zjlzf_AwAA__8l3ZNP) for dozens of counties, and Kerr County officials said they are in contact with summer camps along the Guadalupe River, where floods killed more than 130 people last year.
## ICE Shooting Fallout Widens in Houston
President Trump on Wednesday said ICE agents should [resume most vehicle stops](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZB75DxgCgkvI9tILUdttD631YGT3LDtvf2JfYdMq6VPV9-9j_QDKtD_-wjPO_J3Kusez5cgc68ql7oBlI24Ndti57FQy7Z-rUWaQapR6WBEov1fX4ewVTrqLsx7vTk_TqGy3zbEHnRJ4sN5MynpMyozOeIXa312wHc0XTI160Fppp26IYBRaTBgsOG-FUxGJS73xFjl-Q0v5Xb5ivYXy7PK8MR9N2D_CLMIs53nePrfyukphFqhMIUdhluuXMEsuAbIwC0bA_JYUomxbKUz7Q5iF6-t5_IRcISUKsnE5mjxKpvCWB7zaxTL3XsZ7mhI4LyMMTrrUOzkNk5O2H0LwvU2IQ1dnPE7KmdowCqceT6D8M5t_J_trNv8DAAD__zNXlHs), apparently opposing a pause prompted by fatal shootings in Houston and Maine. The pause followed the July 7 death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, who was [shot by an ICE agent](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O3CAUhZ8Gd4wAe_1TUKRxt2lTWtdwGdAyXAtuxjNvHzlKnmCbUx195-fX5_YJKady_wkPtPwKtBU8W0ZmrBtTLeApJm4NChSmkiin8rUZZUapJqnHzUPK723ovN2VX3SHVk_zoJdlUn0XrXbjspgP0C7Mu5pDmHWv52WEMH_sGPou2QumJj1qrfSgbt6DUb73wbsehr0Xg0KfmOqNIzK-oIX8pifWm6NHl21kPprofwizCrOe53lzObkvE-l3YyqXS5j1miXMmslBFma9MoVZ1fRfIsLzLTOcEkug6vCBheVRsWFxKCseVBm9TEUiNJb_6LJgusedaiTywqxdtf44U86pjZMY1P0BKf8tyt-792nNnwAAAP__GpWRbg) during a stop of his work van in Houston's East End. The Department of Homeland Security says Salgado Araujo rammed a law enforcement vehicle, and the agent fired in self-defense. Attorneys for the three surviving passengers dispute that account, saying no agent was in the van's path and the shots came from the side. The FBI has obtained [a warrant to search the van](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO5CAQBNCvwRkjaGNjBwSXONtLL7TadNtGy8AKuPHOff1p5hc2flKpqv58rB8YYkjHb7yza997XhNfNXJrXNaWS0LKZ2i1YsLUcgo5hvS5goJRKiv1uBKG-FxNR25TNOuOnbaT0fNsVd-dDu0EXrPhfWLkbaCeBw9sFXlAbakL7hWmrB61VtqoGxGCop528j2arRdGMYWWy62d3Pgb6x6f-cHl5vO9i-5s7auK_peARcByXdft88x_XyhgwdKCjyxgee0SsMTsMQpYiJHiUwbPsp45t5COtxZO_7KsGA-kLPctyAcmWRmLP-WFpWBqAhaYBukHtY2otNQ0kTTWb3I2I0sz7bx5mMko7IqjryvEGOpohVHHHUN8F28_u_vh4H8AAAD__9dIlXM). Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare says his office has issued dozens of subpoenas and is "more than prepared" [to file charges](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL_OnDAQxJ8GOiP_CxyFizR0lzYlWuwFnPi8yN477vL0Ed8rfN1IM_ppZn7f5zvEFPP2Cx7o-L3SnPGsCZmxzEwlQ6A9cq2QITPlSCnmv7OWuhdyEKqfA8T0mW0b3CLDqFp0arhZNY6DNO3u_GotKrMEg9Li6vsBx35Qi15v8KM30EZ3weSgeqWksrILAbQMJqzBG7CLaazEEJlKxzsyvqGu6UMvLJ2nR5vcznzUxvxs9NTo6TzPzi_1WnH5jZ4u2ehpp2dlyuIoVNE_mYqIHkXdiTjmTSQqmP-RqJA2CCSgwPMPiaPgAQWDYBJLuYJ-h7LhhWyLC8cZU4q1HxortwfE9NWKv_fly-n_AQAA__8F5o3_) if it finds criminal wrongdoing. Federal officials have not named the agent who fired.
## Paxton Investigates LinkedIn Over 'Ghost Jobs'
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton opened an [investigation into LinkedIn](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O5CAUhE-DM1r82NgEDjZxNptuaAHvuf22MbSAac_cfuWW9gQTVVCqT_rqz8f64ShSuv92B87ta8trwrNGbA3L2nJJDvJOrVaXXGo5UY6UHqsSynAxcmlWcBS_176D2QuwssNZjlMvrR2F7vbZS21wkDiBgCEIbzUgDJNBsHYI09DRfMHEKI2UQvbiBuCUAA0bBO16r1kvEKjlcms7NvxydYvf-YXlFvLRxXlv7VmZ_sXUwtRynuftETC111UztbjSKERkarnMmFpiDi4ytbxR_5O7O7_MECjxzT2QH1QjOqB053-zr_xZ8KDPg9dPX0Mhj-UaK2O5H0BrAMvReMP7wVhuBz1yCCPKMIH049aVGZ4nxUjVjKwX98NRfAu0n93-mtW_AAAA__8RBJgW) over claims that the platform advertised and profited from fake job listings, known as "ghost jobs," that were shown to paying Premium subscribers. His office issued a [Civil Investigative Demand](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAMQL8GuqAkMGQoUlwz3V57JTJrA74JCUp8MPP3J1Z3X7CdZT1Z7_nXx_gBHDguP2EjL685jZHOEkiE8igpR8C0spQCEaKkyClwfI5W215pp0w_InB4j12NftI4mJq8cffODIPTbb36YXaT0_cb3cwdiCwNdGsdkqXpNgy9rtlfx7QzvTHadLpBBKuxxRk_W-imtuo0IUvKjawk9IIyh3c6KDefaauDX0X2UrU_Kvuo7OM8z-YLArn06b1QpAyhWdJR2cdVV9lHpkBQ6Br_c-ofqJ4U1Q4vSVFxPKgILyBU1BVOyFEBHpSFC8dFzfAkBRHVxiUQ4LX7nSaV9j1l-RNZmEqdPe4nh8Cld1Wnlw04fNnL935-ePs3AAD__wZEnjM) for documents on LinkedIn's advertising, verification practices, and Premium subscriptions, which run $39.99 to $69.99 per month. The office says LinkedIn does not independently verify the hiring status of most listings. Independent studies estimate ghost jobs may account for one-fifth to one-third of online job postings, according to the attorney general's office. name: Jace Yarbrough
subject: I am fighting a great evil
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Yarbrough for Congress
body:
I am fighting a great evil, and I cannot stop.

| ["For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil."](https://trk.email.gopnewsnow._JOESTA0psM68F4qQA)[Ephesians 6:12](https://trk.email.gopnewsnow.)
Friend,
Kneeling in prayer a few weeks ago, it hit me plainly. I am fighting a great evil, and I cannot stop.
I'm Jace Yarbrough - candidate for Congress.
[Three facts shape my life: I am a Christian, a husband, and a father of five.](https://trk.email.gopnewsnow.)
I also served in the Air Force, where I saw how Biden's COVID mandates had nothing to do with defending this country and everything to do with control. Twice, I stood up to my own chain of command to defend my faith.
It cost me, but it showed me who we're up against.
As a constitutional lawyer, I have fought for first responders forced to choose between their jobs and their conscience, and for minors targeted by abortion providers.
My wife Elizabeth and I even founded a Christian school because we refused to hand our kids over to a system that no longer shares our values.
America is in a battle between good and evil. Between freedom and godless communism, fighting to own our kids, our conscience, and our future.
I won't pretend I'm not afraid sometimes. But silence is how evil wins.
[I'm fighting to change this broken system once and for all. ](https://trk.email.gopnewsnow.)
[Sadly, nothing seems to cost more these days than running for public office. The honest truth is, I grew up with very little, and don't have bags of dark money like my opponent. ](https://trk.email.gopnewsnow._1Aan5hz9g)
[My filing deadline to take this message to DC hits Friday at midnight, and I need real strength to win this.](https://trk.email.gopnewsnow.)
[Whatever you can give, $25, $50, $100, is an act of faith that this nation is still worth saving. Every hour we wait, the other side gets louder.](https://trk.email.gopnewsnow._m2CAO75wcw)
You will be what makes my race. I thank you in advance and leave you with this:

I know who goes before us, and I know we were not made to be afraid.

name: Adam Kinzinger
subject: I wanted you to hear this from me first
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| Team, this is former Congressman Adam Kinzinger.

The average working-class American plays by the rules, pays their taxes, doesn't cheat, doesn't steal... then watches the President of the United States and his closest allies do all of those things and face zero consequences.

What does that tell them about our political system?

**It tells them it's rigged.**

Here’s the truth: we can’t fix that cynicism with a hope poster.

We can fix it by electing people who will actually do something about it: brave Democrats who will stand up to MAGA extremism, hold politicians accountable, and put our country before politics.

That's exactly why I just launched my new PAC, Back the Bold.

**Our mission is to support Democrats with the courage to say what needs to be said and do what needs to be done to hold Trump and his administration accountable.**

Not the ones who wait. Not the ones who waver.**The bold ones.**

Principle has to mean something. Honor and integrity have to mean something. And if we want different leaders, we have to help elect them up and down the ballot in every election from here on out.

We’re all-in to elect leaders like James Talarico in Texas, who’s running to flip the Lone Star State blue and defeat Trump crony Ken Paxton. Or Annie Andrews in South Carolina, who is fighting to unseat Lindsey Graham for good.

[I’m no stranger to this fight. I’ve been speaking out about Donald Trump and his abuses of power for years. I know what courage looks and feels like, but I need your support to power this fight. Will you split a donation between Back the Bold and the Voter Protection Project to help us elect leaders who will stand up to Trump?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/117927?t=6&akid=26399%2E878179%2E_CAbPk) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Back the Bold and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $7 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/117928?t=7&akid=26399%2E878179%2E_CAbPk)

Friends, **While my opponent seeks endorsements from Washington’s most radical politicians like Bernie Sanders, Pete Buttigieg, and Elizabeth Warren, I am honored to earn the support of the people who know our community best.** The endorsements that mean the most to me are those from the local elected officials, community leaders, and grassroots supporters who work every day to make the Greater Lehigh Valley and Poconos stronger. These are the people who understand the challenges our families, businesses, first responders, farmers, and workers face because they live alongside the people they represent.I'm proud to stand with the local leaders who have dedicated their lives to serving our communities. Their confidence in me reflects the work we’ve done and results we've achieved together—helping constituents, bringing federal resources back to our district, and fighting for policies that improve the lives of the people of Pennsylvania's Seventh District.As your Congressman, I will continue to work for every resident of PA-7, regardless of political party. Whether you're a Republican, Democrat, or Independent, my job is to represent you. At the end of the day, the endorsements I value most are those from the leaders chosen by the people of our communities and, most importantly, the trust placed in me by the people of Pennsylvania's Seventh District.Thank you for your continued support.**Ryan Mackenzie
** Member of Congress, Pennsylvania's 7th District

| Peter, it happened slowly.

I moved to Iowa more than two decades ago, and before I knew it, "ope!" made its way into my vocabulary. If you're not from around here, "ope!" is basically the Midwest's "oops." You say it when you accidentally spill your coffee, bump into someone at the grocery store, or clip the curb while trying to park. It just comes out.

I say "ope!" more often than I'd like to admit. But there's one person who doesn't get to say "ope!" and that's _Mariannette Miller-Meeks._

You don't get to act surprised when the consequences of your own decisions catch up with you. You don't accidentally spend years ignoring your constituents. You don't accidentally vote against Iowa's interests. You don't accidentally support cuts to health care that families rely on. And you certainly don't accidentally spend more time rubbing elbows with wealthy donors and Washington insiders than listening to the people you were elected to represent. **Those were choices she made, and it's exactly why Democrats, independents, and Republicans alike are ready for a representative who actually shows up and puts Iowa first.**

Iowans deserve someone who fights for affordable health care, strong public schools, good-paying jobs, and an economy that works for working families, not someone who's more interested in pleasing party leaders than the people back home.

That's exactly what this campaign is about. I'm running to be the hardest-working representative IA-01 has ever had because this district deserves someone who will put people ahead of politics every single time. **If you believe it's time for a change, will you help us keep building the campaign that can make it happen by pitching in toward our $10,000 mid-month goal? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cb-q3-2026?refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135357892/634011367/-2016015222?refcode=em26_260716_MM3_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260716_MM3_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=5ea48d81-1a81-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZWE0OGQ4MS0xYTgxLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_WI4GA8YdIiSXwLQy-H-CvF1vq_9qIGV5xsTR7nYnaY=)**

body:
The Supreme Court Lets Parties Do Their Job

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-july-16-2026?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/3pNB_f794g_?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)
| | **The Supreme Court Lets Parties Do Their Job****By Justin Riemer, President, USGI** The Supreme Court’s recent [decision](https://us.list-manage.com/wWcJyMg1ANT?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in _NRSC v. FEC_ deserves a few words, even if it’s a little late. The Court struck down, as a violation of the First Amendment, federal legal limits on how much party committees may spend in coordination with their own candidates.
As a lawyer who has advised national and state parties, I welcome the ruling. It always struck me as odd that federal law capped coordinated spending by party committees whose primary purpose is to elect candidates. And the limits included exceptions that exposed how arbitrary they were. State parties could already spend unlimited amounts coordinating with candidates on yard signs, bumper stickers, and palm cards, so long as volunteers distributed them. They could even do mass mailings, subject to convoluted rules that essentially required volunteers to lick stamps and stuff envelopes. Why could a party freely coordinate in these ways but not others? Also, as the Court noted, federal law has long let parties make unlimited _independent_ expenditures supporting candidates, provided staff and vendors involved are firewalled from those handling coordinated spending.
These exceptions left parties struggling to build workable compliance policies, starting with the threshold question of what expenditures are even “coordinated” in the first place. One could plausibly argue that nearly all DNC or RNC spending in a presidential year is coordinated with its nominee. National committees can hire lawyers to manage that legal uncertainty. State parties often cannot, yet they faced this same bewildering compliance regime in addition to layers of state and even local campaign finance laws that govern their fundraising and spending.
Criticism of the decision has been notably muted compared to other campaign finance rulings like _Citizens United_ and _McCutcheon_. Some warn that it will [open up a flood](https://us.list-manage.com/3QuQAG4tABp?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of campaign cash by letting donors evade the lower limits on candidate contributions and route money through parties, which enjoy significantly higher limits. But those criticisms don’t hold up.
The most serious objection is that coordinated spending can function like a direct contribution: a donor _could_ funnel money through the party to a specific candidate and thereby evade the limits on giving to that candidate directly. It is a reasonable concern, but the decision does nothing to enable evasion. _NRSC_ left untouched every tool that, in practice, polices this risk: the limits on what a donor may give a party committee in the first place, the corporate contribution prohibitions, disclosure requirements, and most importantly, earmarking rules that, in many applications, forbid a donor from directing the party to spend on a particular candidate.
I can attest that party officials take earmarking prohibitions extremely seriously, precisely because violating them can carry criminal consequences. No one wants to go to jail, least of all over a campaign finance violation. As a practical matter, parties also try to resist donors dictating how they spend their money, and many major donors are already giving parties the legal maximum. In sum, the conduit scenario argument is largely unfounded.
A cap on coordinated spending was therefore always an over-inclusive and clumsy solution to a problem that practical considerations, contribution limits, source prohibitions, disclosure, and earmarking rules address far more directly.
So much for the risks. What does the ruling actually gain us? As the Court recognized, the ruling has the potential to at least slow the parties’ decline, especially state parties, which are in sad shape both financially and in their degree of political influence. Critics like Rick Hasen [allege](https://us.list-manage.com/15L7h3hjHfU?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the Court engaged in “deregulatory bootstrapping” — using its own earlier overruling of precedent to justify still more change. In the campaign finance context, they point to _Citizens United_ and its progeny for empowering SuperPACs and other nonprofits at the parties’ expense. But the real instigator came earlier when Congress enacted the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act of 2002 (BCRA). BCRA gutted the financial clout of the national party committees by eliminating so-called “soft money,” sharply limited its use by state parties, and inexplicably never indexed state party contribution limits to inflation. Although _Citizens United_ accelerated the process, it was BCRA, well before that 2010 decision, that began driving a larger share of campaign money out of the traditional party apparatus and into the outside groups that are increasingly eclipsing it.
There is relative consensus across the ideological spectrum that strong political party organizations benefit our political system, both because they can help temper polarization and because they remain a pillar of local and state civic life. _NRSC_ will provide parties with a boost at a time they need it most.

| | **Arizona** Pinal County [began replacing](https://us.list-manage.com/VPGEKurZeGG?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) nearly 1,500 Republican primary ballots after a printing error traced to the state voter-registration database vendor affected precinct committeeman races in two precincts. Officials caught similar problems in Cochise and Yuma counties before ballots were mailed.The campaign behind the proposed Free, Fair and Secure Elections Act—a constitutional amendment that would have guaranteed no-excuse mail voting, a right to vote in person on Election Day, and early in-person voting through the Monday before an election—[withheld its signatures](https://us.list-manage.com/11PMY2QIrtP?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a), keeping the measure off the November ballot. Organizers said they gathered roughly 439,000 signatures but declined to submit them rather than provide signer information to “election-denying” county election officials, and said they would instead mount a legal challenge to HCR 2001, the legislature’s referred voter-identification measure.**California** The Los Angeles City Council [pulled](https://us.list-manage.com/ZnDCt90c481?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) from the November ballot a measure that would have allowed noncitizens to vote in city and school district elections, voting unanimously to study the proposal further with the goal of returning it to voters before 2028.The state budget [committed $40 million](https://us.list-manage.com/kLcEyE507VG?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to election administration ahead of the midterms, including $29 million for county staffing, technology, and equipment intended to accelerate ballot counting.**Colorado** Ouray County [accepted ballots online](https://us.list-manage.com/H1bmncreqrb?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) from primary voters unable to vote in person because of wildfires, under a state statute in place since 2014 permitting emergency voting during natural disasters.The U.S. Postal Service has [offered no clear explanation](https://us.list-manage.com/d86pK5ea9Fa?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) for primary ballot delivery delays in Grand County, with some residents reporting they had not received their ballots by Election Day.The legislature’s 2026 session [produced](https://us.list-manage.com/14BQ9eWTqmx?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an omnibus elections bill and seven other enacted election-related laws.**Connecticut** No-excuse absentee voting [took effect](https://us.list-manage.com/DNUGbJU2kgR?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) statewide, implementing the constitutional amendment voters approved to remove the state’s absentee-ballot excuse requirements.The Elections Enforcement Commission [opened an investigation](https://us.list-manage.com/14bWvKZD7Wb?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) into candidate petition pages that went missing from Hamden’s Registrar of Voters Office.**Florida** Florida prosecutors [charged five people](https://us.list-manage.com/1BFCn__YfG8?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a), including two St. Johns County commissioners and a former St. Augustine Beach mayor, over an allegedly unauthorized voter guide distributed during the 2024 Republican primary. The guide allegedly mimicked the county GOP’s official publication, falsely conveyed party endorsements, and omitted required disclaimers. One defendant also faces felony evidence-tampering charges.Maria Matthews, director of the Division of Elections since 2013, is [leaving the post](https://us.list-manage.com/jGglW5a0OAb?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) ahead of this year’s primaries, according to a spokesperson for Secretary of State Cord Byrd. Her last day in the office was June 30, and she will continue assisting the division through July 31.**Georgia** Governor Kemp [signed](https://us.list-manage.com/WPVd1ZTXYuD?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Senate Bill 3EX, extending the QR-code tabulation deadline to 2028, creating a committee to recommend a replacement statewide system, and requiring automatic hand recounts in the top two statewide races when the margin is 0.5% or less.Secretary of State Raffensperger [announced](https://us.list-manage.com/R_DtCG7WYKa?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that a statewide audit found 23 discrepancies among more than 1.1 million ballots, all involving hand-marked ballots.State officials [launched an investigation](https://us.list-manage.com/17nc8cVaNLH?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) into third-party voter-registration mailers sent to deceased Georgians and other ineligible recipients.**Indiana** County officials [revoked the registration](https://us.list-manage.com/lO8FuHmOdSl?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of a longtime naturalized citizen erroneously flagged under the state’s proof-of-citizenship screening laws after a database outage. The voter re-registered by presenting her naturalization paperwork and did not miss the May primary.**Iowa** A tied Runnells City Council special election [will be decided](https://us.list-manage.com/r6UqU5IysFB?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) by drawing names, per state tie-breaking procedure.West Des Moines [ended its use](https://us.list-manage.com/PcOH_AqP6Hm?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of runoff elections, citing cost and low turnout. In its place, the city will use a winner-take-all system for the candidate receiving the highest vote count.**Kentucky** Jefferson County Clerk David Yates [announced a countywide audit](https://us.list-manage.com/SGg8xdamCrH?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of precinct assignments after disclosing that a 2021 clerical error assigned 30 voters to the wrong precinct, preventing several from voting in a state House primary decided by five votes.**Maryland** The Open Meetings Compliance Board [found](https://us.list-manage.com/QwHAK1CTuKT?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that the Charles County Board of Elections violated the Open Meetings Act by failing to adequately disclose the topics it intended to discuss in closed session and the reason for excluding the public from those discussions. The meeting in question involved candidate ballot eligibility.**Michigan** A jury [acquitted](https://us.list-manage.com/12EOwGK7rWS?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a Hamtramck city councilman of felony election-law forgery charges stemming from the 2023 city council election, while convicting him of a misdemeanor for providing a false statement on an absentee-ballot application.Another uncounted ballot [surfaced](https://us.list-manage.com/1JprO5gNvqh?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in Hamtramck, prompting Mayor Adam Alharbi to call for election reform. The discovery comes amid an unresolved dispute over 37 absentee ballots that went uncounted in the November 2025 mayoral election.A resident [filed a recall petition](https://us.list-manage.com/f8xsVCWZAzQ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) against the Antrim County Clerk, whose access to the qualified voter file the state suspended in June. The Board of State Canvassers will review whether the petition’s language meets legal standards.**Minnesota** A [state legislative audit found](https://us.list-manage.com/NGTViEi_KTa?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that, among other errors, counties failed to challenge 16 of 59 registrants flagged as newly incarcerated for felonies and missed statutory deadlines for 45% of applications submitted within 20 days of an election. The audit [ultimately concluded](https://us.list-manage.com/mlIi4t2VhVF?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that Minnesota’s overall voter-registration procedures were generally adequate.**Mississippi** The SHIELD Act [took effect](https://us.list-manage.com/BISIP1GERHx?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a), requiring election officials to check new voter-registration applications against the federal SAVE database. Applicants not found in the database have 30 days to provide proof of citizenship.**Nevada** The Lyon County Clerk-Treasurer’s office [confirmed](https://us.list-manage.com/1CQoHbkL8iX?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that 32 mail ballots cast in the June primary went uncounted after the Postal Service marked them undeliverable, despite correct addressing, and delivered them to the secretary of state’s office weeks after the election. Officials said the ballots would not have changed any race’s outcome. Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar, who placed the blame on USPS, opened an investigation, and the county, which has documented more than 200 mail-related problems since 2023, requested assistance from the governor’s and congressional offices.**New Jersey** The state [enacted](https://us.list-manage.com/BOh6k4uUdmG?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a state-level voting rights act, becoming the eleventh state with such a law. clean_body: The Supreme Court Lets Parties Do Their Job | | | | | | | | | The Supreme Court Lets Parties Do Their JobBy Justin Riemer, President, USGI The Supreme Court’s recent in NRSC v. FEC deserves a few words, even if it’s a little late. The Court struck down, as a violation of the First Amendment, federal legal limits on how much party committees may spend in coordination with their own candidates. As a lawyer who has advised national and state parties, I welcome the ruling. It always struck me as odd that federal law capped coordinated spending by party committees whose primary purpose is to elect candidates. And the limits included exceptions that exposed how arbitrary they were. State parties could already spend unlimited amounts coordinating with candidates on yard signs, bumper stickers, and palm cards, so long as volunteers distributed them. They could even do mass mailings, subject to convoluted rules that essentially required volunteers to lick stamps and stuff envelopes. Why could a party freely coordinate in these ways but not others? Also, as the Court noted, federal law has long let parties make unlimited independent expenditures supporting candidates, provided staff and vendors involved are firewalled from those handling coordinated spending. These exceptions left parties struggling to build workable compliance policies, starting with the threshold question of what expenditures are even “coordinated” in the first place. One could plausibly argue that nearly all DNC or RNC spending in a presidential year is coordinated with its nominee. National committees can hire lawyers to manage that legal uncertainty. State parties often cannot, yet they faced this same bewildering compliance regime in addition to layers of state and even local campaign finance laws that govern their fundraising and spending. Criticism of the decision has been notably muted compared to other campaign finance rulings like Citizens United and McCutcheon. Some warn that it will of campaign cash by letting donors evade the lower limits on candidate contributions and route money through parties, which enjoy significantly higher limits. But those criticisms don’t hold up. The most serious objection is that coordinated spending can function like a direct contribution: a donor could funnel money through the party to a specific candidate and thereby evade the limits on giving to that candidate directly. It is a reasonable concern, but the decision does nothing to enable evasion. NRSC left untouched every tool that, in practice, polices this risk: the limits on what a donor may give a party committee in the first place, the corporate contribution prohibitions, disclosure requirements, and most importantly, earmarking rules that, in many applications, forbid a donor from directing the party to spend on a particular candidate. I can attest that party officials take earmarking prohibitions extremely seriously, precisely because violating them can carry criminal consequences. No one wants to go to jail, least of all over a campaign finance violation. As a practical matter, parties also try to resist donors dictating how they spend their money, and many major donors are already giving parties the legal maximum. In sum, the conduit scenario argument is largely unfounded. A cap on coordinated spending was therefore always an over-inclusive and clumsy solution to a problem that practical considerations, contribution limits, source prohibitions, disclosure, and earmarking rules address far more directly. So much for the risks. What does the ruling actually gain us? As the Court recognized, the ruling has the potential to at least slow the parties’ decline, especially state parties, which are in sad shape both financially and in their degree of political influence. Critics like Rick Hasen the Court engaged in “deregulatory bootstrapping” — using its own earlier overruling of precedent to justify still more change. In the campaign finance context, they point to Citizens United and its progeny for empowering SuperPACs and other nonprofits at the parties’ expense. But the real instigator came earlier when Congress enacted the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act of 2002 (BCRA). BCRA gutted the financial clout of the national party committees by eliminating so-called “soft money,” sharply limited its use by state parties, and inexplicably never indexed state party contribution limits to inflation. Although Citizens United accelerated the process, it was BCRA, well before that 2010 decision, that began driving a larger share of campaign money out of the traditional party apparatus and into the outside groups that are increasingly eclipsing it. There is relative consensus across the ideological spectrum that strong political party organizations benefit our political system, both because they can help temper polarization and because they remain a pillar of local and state civic life. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

name: Free Speech Daily Sponsor
subject: Is the UN about to seize 400,000 acres of American soil?
body:
The only thing standing between the UN’s 400,000-acre power grab and American soil is one decision.
---
| | | | | |
---
| | | | | [View in browser](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAcgmKlS6IrjFMRsCDnFphzAV1UZfJt0mzYNCkbM18S43M_-2tYcguOZXK-ZbVZAahblQtS4XE3hR_8L35gPo3hwchav4Dz0gCAqm "View in Browser")
---
_**A Special Message from our Sponsor**_ _Please note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of_ _Free Speech Daily_ _and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily_ _._
---
| *|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | | | [ ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAcgmKlS7XX6tsboGtP0N_C9LW-NrVZC425ClBqEgJX_dcR3sBedwRh2QBxdL1FPD3O5ULYkBrY1Jert4I-7Sh33UcFl6NgRUWhrO)
---
| | Dear Fellow Patriot,

On July 19, a committee of 21 foreign governments gavels into session in Busan, South Korea – and somewhere in the days that follow, they’ll decide whether a 400,000-acre stretch of Georgia answers to them.

Not to Georgia. Not to America.

To _them_ – the United Nations.

And don’t kid yourself that it stops at one swamp. Hand the UN 400,000 acres of Georgia and you’ve handed them the precedent – the next piece of America comes easier, and the one after that easier still.

I’m Craig Rucker, President of CFACT – the Committee for a Constructive Tomorrow – and I want to give you a frank update on what the United Nations is actually up to right now.

Last weekend, you and I were lighting fireworks for America’s 250th birthday – a quarter of a millennium since a handful of farmers and shopkeepers told the most powerful empire on earth to take its crown and its tax collectors and pound sand.

**And now, before the smoke clears, the UN’s culture bureaucrats want to plant their flag in the Okefenokee Swamp.**

They don’t call it a flag, of course. They call it a “World Heritage Site” – a designation of “outstanding universal value.” (Translation: it’s not really yours anymore.)

The UN swears it would “only monitor” this swath of American land. (Right – the way a fox “only monitors” the henhouse.) Ask the folks in Charlton, Ware, and Clinch counties in Georgia what “monitor” means.

They’re the ones who’d wake up to find their hunting land, their timber, their own backyards redrawn as a “buffer zone” to “protect” a swamp that’s been doing just fine on its own since before there was a United Nations to mismanage it.

No hunting. No logging. No pulling weeds. No say. That’s the “universal value” on offer.

[**Will you please add your name to CFACT’s Declaration of Independence from the UN to tell President Trump and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to pull this nomination off the table before the July 19 deadline**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAcgmKlS8zSaoDI1rVxs_g0BWCStjQbOjtr5OBzxZmjZ8AbYlfkKC5IUw-mXi8LiX1UxjdWTYHfp6BgUa1T7AvJzl9Kd8_Dwta_G2)?
[**Add My Name to the Declaration >>**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAcgmKlS9GxkhcNFsXitWCTf8jPVFxOzJlBN1QpAQxe7wMM8UvDg52zhNYqyawj7zEel6j6sdThRJw9LGOnvotVftUHocnIceHqAZ)
So how did we get here? A midnight gift in January 2025.

The Okefenokee sat on a UN “tentative list” for some 40 years, going nowhere – until the Biden administration, just before clearing out its desks, rammed through the nomination without so much as a phone call to the people who actually live there.

**A parting gift to the UN – from the same crew that spent four years handing out pieces of American sovereignty to anyone who asked.**

And the outfit advising the UN on whether to bless it?

The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) – the global green bureaucracy whose own network brags about cramming climate “education” into the Paris accord that Trump already tore up.

This was never about alligators and peat moss. **It’s about handing a chunk of America to the climate agenda’s permanent government – the one nobody elected and nobody can fire.**

President Trump already walked America out of UNESCO – one of 66 international outfits he’s shown the door to, including the UN’s climate convention itself. Good.

But walking out of UNESCO alone doesn’t stop this.

**The nomination rides a separate track, and the United States is still bound to the “World Heritage Convention.”**

Which means unless Secretary Burgum formally rescinds it, those 21 foreign governments get the final word on American soil – whether we’re members of their little club or not.

One signature stands between the UN and the Okefenokee – Secretary Burgum’s, on an order pulling this nomination off the table. _That’s the whole fight, in a single stroke of a pen_.

This is exactly the fight CFACT was built for.

Our team went to Folkston, Georgia – cameras rolling – and sat down with the county commissioners the UN never bothered to consult, and put their warnings on the record while the national press looked the other way.

**We’re also one of the only conservative outfits holding official NGO observer status at the United Nations – which means when they convene, we have the standing to be in the room and fight them to their faces.**

That’s the difference between a think tank and a DO tank. And because we don’t take one dime of taxpayer money, there isn’t a globalist on this earth who can buy us off or shut us up.

_The good news?_ This fight is winnable, and the momentum is ours.

Three counties have already passed ordinances against it. When the UN’s own advisors held their little meeting down in Folkston, it did not go the way they planned.

America has walked away from UNESCO before – under Reagan, and again under Trump. The pattern is hard to miss: when Americans actually show up, the globalists lose.

So let’s show up.

[**Add your name to the Declaration today – and then chip in $25, $50, or $100 to keep CFACT’s boots on the ground for the next land grab, because there is always a next one**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAcgmKlS-uEB4HLkPfstCkX8PVeXz8jjhkJVmjXJ9QC-nkOx4sKpMDdyBnhatt1IvEBRgpwFi_qbxpwUa8AhycwHlVC2W8CWdncTU).

Two hundred and fifty years ago, we declared our independence from a faraway power that thought it owned us.

It’s time to do it again.

For American sovereignty,

Craig Rucker
President

P.S. – Twenty-one foreign governments are about to vote on a piece of Georgia, fifteen days after we celebrate 250 years of telling distant powers exactly where to put their opinions about our land. [**Add your name before July 19 – and let’s make this Independence Day mean something**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAcgmKlS_Wi7ozeNBB-uyXlRChxdYB7pxOCLDAJGutchU_yL9COcWRk2kDgARI7NZ4kOA8a8UlzhpAB11bGJmwoVYyajqzlM0G39K).
[**Add My Name to the Declaration >>**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAcgmKlTAWtbIKHQKipsRGcXQmaxf2mgvuy41KDvBMfUwY97WuedwB223oseUFqmVf-Ni1CNwonfYm2EKJTRQKKlKStTsK3fhZ9B-)

This was never about alligators and peat moss. It’s about handing a chunk of America to the climate agenda’s permanent government – the one nobody elected and nobody can fire. President Trump already walked America out of UNESCO – one of 66 international outfits he’s shown the door to, including the UN’s climate convention itself. Good. But walking out of UNESCO alone doesn’t stop this. The nomination rides a separate track, and the United States is still bound to the “World Heritage Convention.” Which means unless Secretary Burgum formally rescinds it, those 21 foreign governments get the final word on American soil – whether we’re members of their little club or not. One signature stands between the UN and the Okefenokee – Secretary Burgum’s, on an order pulling this nomination off the table. That’s the whole fight, in a single stroke of a pen. This is exactly the fight CFACT was built for. Our team went to Folkston, Georgia – cameras rolling – and sat down with the county commissioners the UN never bothered to consult, and put their warnings on the record while the national press looked the other way. We’re also one of the only conservative outfits holding official NGO observer status at the United Nations – which means when they convene, we have the standing to be in the room and fight them to their faces. That’s the difference between a think tank and a DO tank. And because we don’t take one dime of taxpayer money, there isn’t a globalist on this earth who can buy us off or shut us up. The good news? This fight is winnable, and the momentum is ours. Three counties have already passed ordinances against it. When the UN’s own advisors held their little meeting down in Folkston, it did not go the way they planned. America has walked away from UNESCO before – under Reagan, and again under Trump. The pattern is hard to miss: when Americans actually show up, the globalists lose. So let’s show up. . Two hundred and fifty years ago, we declared our independence from a faraway power that thought it owned us. It’s time to do it again. For American sovereignty, Craig Rucker President P.S. – Twenty-one foreign governments are about to vote on a piece of Georgia, fifteen days after we celebrate 250 years of telling distant powers exactly where to put their opinions about our land. . - Copyright © 2026 Committee for a Constructive Tomorrow (CFACT), All rights reserved. She knew the sport. But she never expected her opponent to be a male who identifies as female. Visibly distressed, Kallie let herself be pinned just to make the match stop. She came off the mat and ran to her mother in tears. Two days later, Stephanie reported the assault in writing, with video, to Kallie's coaches. One of them said she hadn't known the opponent was male and promised to follow up. Then ... almost total silence. Washington law requires officials to report an assault to law enforcement within 48 hours. Kallie's school waited 53 days--and only acted after a journalist started asking questions. Kallie and her mother are not staying quiet. With Alliance Defending Freedom representing them in court at no cost to them, they've filed a federal lawsuit to make girls sports safe again--so that no other girl is sent out the way Kallie was. This is the fight ADF is taking on across the country: keeping men out of women's sports and defending the girls who've been forced to compete against them. Kallie is why it matters. Your gift today funds ADF's fight to keep men out of women's sports. Sincerely, Julie Marie Blake Senior Counsel, Regulatory Litigation Alliance Defending Freedom | Alliance Defending Freedom 15100 N. 90th Street, Scottsdale, Arizona 85260

body:
I’m proud to support these three working-class candidates for Congress.
#
I’ve got some big news, Peter.
**I’m proud to announce Small Town PAC’s very first round of 2026 endorsements:**
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260716-1.EYJf9d&amount=5&refcode=em20260716-866&t=2&akid=866%2E34582%2Eg7J5Vs)
**[If you’re ready to join me in supporting these three candidates for Congress, fuel our work with a grassroots contribution now →](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260716-1.EYJf9d&amount=5&refcode=em20260716-866&t=3&akid=866%2E34582%2Eg7J5Vs)**
I launched Small Town PAC back in April to put power back into the hands of our neighbors and help Democrats expand the map in small towns and rural communities across the country. Now, with your help, we’re putting that mission into action and working to win some elections this November.
So far, the Small Town PAC 2026 Slate includes:
**Jake Johnson** — a teacher in my old district in Minnesota.
**Sarah Trone Garriott** — a minister and State Senator in Iowa.
**Rachel Wallace** — a public servant in Pennsylvania.
You know, every single one of these candidates has a real understanding of the struggles working people face. Each of them knows what it’s like to sit at the kitchen table and wonder how they’re going to cover the next medical bill, fill up their gas tank, or budget for their family’s next grocery trip.
They’re regular people, with fresh ideas and first-hand experience dealing with the problems facing small towns across America. They aren’t running to please consultants, lobbies, or political insiders — they’re running to make life affordable again for working families.
Starting this November, we’re ready to kick the billionaires and tech bros out of D.C. and replace them with working-class people who understand the real issues facing our communities.
**All four of these Democrats are running in competitive red-to-blue races in places that too often get ignored** , like Southern Minnesota (including my old town of Mankato), Des Moines, and Pottsville.
**[This is what the next generation of leadership looks like, Peter. If you believe these working-class leaders can do a heck of a lot better than the billionaires running things now, chip in $5 to power our work from now through Election Day.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260716-1.EYJf9d&amount=5&refcode=em20260716-866&t=4&akid=866%2E34582%2Eg7J5Vs)**

Let’s get to work and WIN!
With gratitude,
Tim

| Our midmonth deadline is tonight — and the stakes just changed.
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=9939%2E5257348%2E8uTf2Z)
Derek, Last Thursday, Donald Trump fired every remaining commissioner of the federal agency that helps states run secure elections. By email. Effective immediately. Four months before the midterms. Days earlier, his Justice Department announced it's deploying election monitors into battleground states and Democratic strongholds — and threatened election officials in all 50 states with criminal prosecution. **Fired the referees. Sent in his own watchers. Threatened the people who count the votes.** I spent years as a federal prosecutor. I know a pattern of intent when I see one. This isn't election security — it's an attempt to seize control of our elections before a single ballot is cast. #### Two hundred thirty-seven years ago this week, the people of Paris stormed the Bastille.
Quick history check: the fortress held seven prisoners. Seven. Nobody stormed it for the inventory. They stormed it because it stood for a simple arrangement--the aristocracy does whatever it wants, and everyone else pays for it.
We know a little something about that arrangement in 2026, don't we?
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.ApRvNW80XC-whDB3GOglISi5-a3C05MAWFUJXarAKTI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=207300056)
Marie Antoinette never actually said "let them eat cake," by the way. But "let them eat eight-dollar eggs while we cut their health care" is, more or less word for word, the operating policy of today's predator class. At least the French aristocrats had the decency to be embarrassed.
Ours post about it.
[Through Sunday, every Blue Amp subscription is 25% off.](https://substack.com/redirect/5176aa3c-99c5-4dd6-8832-0a36f5798ff3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) That's the whole pitch: independent progressive media, no billionaire owner, one week at Bastille pricing.
[Join The Fight! 25% Off](https://substack.com/redirect/5176aa3c-99c5-4dd6-8832-0a36f5798ff3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Happy Bastille Day week, and pour one out for the French team in the World Cup (although I'm pouring one out for England).

# **Far-left Michigan senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed releases partial tax return showing top 1% income**
Abdul El-Sayed **[released two pages of his 2025 tax return](https://substack.com/redirect/59344968-8700-4d65-be47-952bf3ba77d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Tuesday revealing $686,069 in total income -- placing him in Michigan's top 1% of earners, roughly 10 times the state's median household income of $68,500. # **IRS data shows New York and California dominate nation 's taxpayer exodus**
All ten counties with the largest net losses of taxpayers to other states were located in California and New York, **[according to the latest IRS migration data.](https://substack.com/redirect/8c20a68a-eb6a-4a59-a804-ba798da441c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Los Angeles County led the nation, losing nearly 17,500 tax filers who took roughly $1.9 billion in income with them. Queens, the Bronx, Orange County, and Suffolk County rounded out the top five.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8c20a68a-eb6a-4a59-a804-ba798da441c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The destinations tell a clear story.** The fastest-growing counties for incoming tax filers were Maricopa County, Arizona; Harris County, Texas; and Clark County, Nevada -- all in lower-tax Sun Belt states. Economists say residents are voting with their feet, fleeing high taxes and regulation for states with lower costs of living and no income tax.
* **Manhattan bucked the trend in one notable way** -- gaining more new filers than any other county nationally while simultaneously losing nearly $1 billion in adjusted gross income, suggesting wealthier residents are leaving and lower earners are taking their place.

* * *
# **Tim Walz defends pardoning child rapist after Trump admin deports him anyway**
Minnesota Governor Tim Walz **[doubled down Tuesday on his decision to pardon Tou Lue Vang,](https://substack.com/redirect/7364913a-fcc0-4b08-b194-3f1475c3eff6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a Laotian national convicted of repeatedly sexually assaulting a 10-year-old girl over two years beginning in 2002. Walz questioned whether the Trump administration's subsequent deportation made anyone safer, suggesting people shouldn't be "judged by our worst day" and raising concerns about the children Vang left behind.
