**From Drop Site:**
* **[Iran Sent Message to JD Vance Warning that Kushner and Witkoff Were "Abusing" Their Inside Access to Negotiations](https://substack.com/redirect/036b7793-e52b-40a0-826f-0b751c0290f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

_U.S.[ hits](https://substack.com/redirect/de9e904b-b5a8-4d4b-a950-cfa0ef7be08a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran with fifth day of renewed attacks. Iran [responds](https://substack.com/redirect/4cd90de1-a6d6-4bf3-9909-c9547cbd104d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), hitting U.S. bases in the Gulf. Iran [calls](https://substack.com/redirect/ce4c7400-c044-4a39-a751-3a8b9383396b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Hormuz its "red line." Pricey U.S. drone [shot down](https://substack.com/redirect/9de7e395-72ae-4d9b-a644-4a2fadc1b538?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [goes](https://substack.com/redirect/b792854d-1d0d-4357-acba-0d67f878e312?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Doha. [WSJ](https://substack.com/redirect/dfbd54ab-7b08-44a5-af40-de38b82f900d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): President Donald Trump favors expanding military operations against Iran. Israeli ceasefire violations [continue](https://substack.com/redirect/edd48c3c-5d1d-4df4-a9aa-aa14e1476663?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) across southern Lebanon. Israel reaffirms [plans](https://substack.com/redirect/24fa1dfd-bedd-49df-8b96-57fff29bf166?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to maintain occupation in parts of Lebanon, Gaza, and Syria. Three Palestinians [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/16916832-17a1-43b3-97bb-30898cfd2d6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Israeli strikes on Thursday. Gaza government [files](https://substack.com/redirect/c4b6baa3-13f5-4a82-be78-aa7f94827c41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) complaint against UN official, says statement provided "pretext" for deadly Israeli strike. Israel [approves](https://substack.com/redirect/460cdcf1-ae41-4d21-a391-d2f1a9efae6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $330 million to expand road network for West Bank settlements. Colombia's incoming government to [restore](https://substack.com/redirect/2e345661-3108-4d65-9f89-b22634c3755f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) full ties with Israel, open embassy in Jerusalem. Amendment to cut State Department aid to Israel [fails](https://substack.com/redirect/e0431529-5ca6-4cab-aa16-18a48d7158e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in U.S. House, but prominent Democrats back the cut. Groups [sue](https://substack.com/redirect/556cf119-84ae-4630-b687-57626c51ff0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Trump administration over ICC sanctions. Pentagon [weighs](https://substack.com/redirect/6d57a367-6135-4a62-bfe6-3da124a88237?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Cuba military options as Iran war resumes. House GOP unveils budget to fund Iran war. Report [finds](https://substack.com/redirect/5046aeca-6535-4c5a-9b79-4ea90d3c9f20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) widespread abuse allegations at Texas ICE facility. Venezuelan man [becomes](https://substack.com/redirect/c36cdb12-58f2-41db-a5e8-f4d9560e5019?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 22nd ICE detainee to die this year. Vice President JD Vance [admits](https://substack.com/redirect/7c34c882-a855-4e52-84b6-2fb685272106?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Trump administration mishandled Epstein files release. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum [rejects](https://substack.com/redirect/a179ddfb-59f2-4cd3-96c9-1abd51b998ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) DEA claim of cartel ties to Mexican government. U.S. [imposes](https://substack.com/redirect/a0f3a9a2-9fcf-4d07-b0b1-b1773f7ec909?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 25% tariffs on Brazil, exempts key exports. More than 500 [feared](https://substack.com/redirect/d3ab8c8f-f12e-4f62-bde5-c795c9a72d60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) dead after boats sink off Myanmar. Russian nuclear plant chief [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/c6b330fc-905d-4059-8bc2-a7e3d504059a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in drone strike. Recent militia massacres [kill](https://substack.com/redirect/efee59bc-be04-4710-9581-615f6e2c8e7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over 200 in Eastern Congo._

# Iran and Ceasefire
* **U.S. hits Iran with fifth day of renewed attacks:** U.S. forces [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/de9e904b-b5a8-4d4b-a950-cfa0ef7be08a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two waves of strikes against Iran on Wednesday, targeting Iranian military capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz, the country's Central Command announced, with the earlier wave of strikes hitting Iran's Tunb Island.
* CENTCOM [said](https://substack.com/redirect/0d76f5e3-bb76-41bc-85cf-80c1a958da25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the second wave targeted military installations in the south and on the Persian Gulf coast, including Bandar Abbas.
* U.S. strikes hit Ahvaz in Iran's South, according to Iran's WANA. The U.S. launched multiple projectiles that landed in the vicinity of Shahid Baqaei Hospital, a hospital which specializes in the treatment of children with cancer.
* The hospital's director confirmed that 211 of its patients, including vulnerable children undergoing chemotherapy and those on ventilators, had to be urgently evacuated to nearby facilities like Golestan and Shafa hospitals. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei condemned the attack in a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/09eae08e-c875-4619-97cd-47d229b85afb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, calling it "barbaric" and a "cowardly war crime against the most innocent of human beings."
* U.S. strikes also hit sites in the north, with one hitting a storage facility near Semnan and the city's civilian airport, according to Al Jazeera.
* Other strikes were [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/3126980a-0daf-4981-8d0c-0724fa0ccce8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Khondab, Andimeshk, Qeshm, Sirik, Konarak, Rask, and Chabahar.
* U.S. forces also fired missiles into the smokestack of a Curaçao-flagged oil tanker, the Belma, disabling it as it sailed toward Iran's Kharg Island, Central Command said Wednesday, the first commercial ship the U.S. has struck since its blockade resumed.
* CENTCOM also attempted to wave away the damage its strikes had already done to civilian infrastructure within the country, denying in a Thursday statement that it had targeted a civilian wheat storage facility in Hoveyzeh on Tuesday.
* **Iran responds, hitting U.S. bases in the Gulf:** Iran [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/4cd90de1-a6d6-4bf3-9909-c9547cbd104d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fresh missile and drone attacks on U.S. military sites in Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan early Thursday, hours after another round of American strikes on Iran.
* In Kuwait, Iran reported hitting radar systems, a Patriot air-defense battery, and fuel storage at the Ali al-Salem Air Base, according to state broadcaster IRIB. Kuwaiti officials reported engaging "hostile" attacks with at least 4 cruise missiles and 21 drones intercepted.
* Iran also said it struck U.S. facilities at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, where the Interior Ministry sounded air-raid sirens Thursday morning and urged residents to head to the nearest safe place.
* Jordan intercepted 8 Iranian missiles on Thursday, the state news agency Petra said. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it fired two waves of ballistic missiles at U.S. air bases in Jordan, claiming they had been used to launch strikes on Iran, including the attack near a children's cancer hospital.
* Kuwait's army also [said](https://substack.com/redirect/69329207-9689-4cf7-a08d-332cea930f98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its air defenses were intercepting another wave of "hostile drone attacks" on Thursday.
* **Iran calls Hormuz its "red line," vows devastating retaliation if U.S. hits infrastructure:** Ibrahim Zolfaghari, a spokesman for Iran's Khatam Al-Anbiya Joint Headquarters, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/ce4c7400-c044-4a39-a751-3a8b9383396b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a statement on Wednesday that "under no circumstances and in no way" would Iran permit America "to interfere in the Strait of Hormuz," calling this Iran's "unimpeachable red line."
* Zolfaghari added that Iran would pound the U.S.' Gulf allies "with steel blows" until "no trace" remains "as if" these countries "never existed from the beginning," should the U.S. carry out its threats against civilian infrastructure.
* This follows comments by President Donald Trump threatening to strike Iran's power plants and bridges next week unless Tehran returns to negotiations. "Next week it gets really bad for them," Trump told Fox News. "We're going to knock out all their power plants. We're going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate."
* Trump later said Iran "better behave" and told a defence summit that Tehran "wants to settle so badly," adding that Washington would decide whether to reach an agreement "or if we just finish it off."
* **Iran told Vance Witkoff, Kushner were "abusing" their inside access to negotiations: **During U.S.-Iran talks in Lake Lucerne, Switzerland, in late June, Iranian negotiators sent a private message to Vice President JD Vance through an intermediary warning that President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were undermining efforts to turn the June 17 framework into a lasting agreement, a senior Iranian official told Drop Site.
* According to the official, Iran accused the pair of exploiting insider knowledge of the negotiations for financial gain and raised concerns over leaks by Kushner to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
* The official added that Iran requested a share of what it estimated were $9 billion in profits from alleged market manipulation. The White House denied the claims, with spokesperson Anna Kelly saying no such message had been transmitted "to the United States," and accusing Drop Site of being "filled with hate for America." **Read the full story by Jeremy Scahill and Ryan Grim[ here](https://substack.com/redirect/036b7793-e52b-40a0-826f-0b751c0290f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Watch [Fox News discuss](https://substack.com/redirect/d32b133d-9665-4c6c-9466-f17c7e8522ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the story.**
* **Pricey U.S. drone shot down:** Another US MQ-9 drone, costing between $30-40 million, was [shot down](https://substack.com/redirect/9de7e395-72ae-4d9b-a644-4a2fadc1b538?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday, Iran's Fars news agency reported, in Iran's southwest.
* In mid-May 2026 briefings to the Senate Armed Services Committee, defense officials testified that the active fleet of MQ-9 drones had dwindled significantly, plummeting to roughly 135 operational units, down from a baseline of 189 aircraft.
* The U.S. lost $1 billion worth of these drones in the first part of the war, according to their testimony.

* **Araghchi goes to Doha:** Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [traveled](https://substack.com/redirect/b792854d-1d0d-4357-acba-0d67f878e312?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Doha on Thursday to "meet Qatari officials and to express his condolences" to Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani following the death of Qatar's former emir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, according to Araghchi's official Telegram channel.
* The visit may also be a sign that diplomatic channels remain open through Qatar, a key mediator in U.S.-Iran talks.
* Pakistan, another key mediator, said Thursday it remains committed to the memorandum reached last month despite the collapse of the initial pause in hostilities. "While the implementation of the MOU is facing challenges," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said, "Pakistan will continue to encourage all sides to end violence and resume technical-level talks."
* **WSJ: Trump favors expanding military operations against Iran** : Trump is leaning toward expanding U.S. military operations against Iran after briefings from top aides, including options to seize Kharg Island and bomb the fortified Pickaxe Mountain site, U.S. officials [told](https://substack.com/redirect/dfbd54ab-7b08-44a5-af40-de38b82f900d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Wall Street Journal.
* Trump is also considering airstrikes against civilian energy infrastructure, according to the report.

* In the Nabatieh district, Israeli warplanes [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/edd48c3c-5d1d-4df4-a9aa-aa14e1476663?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two airstrikes on the outskirts of the Al-Deir neighborhood in Nabatieh al-Fawqa at around 2 p.m., followed about 45 minutes later by a drone strike [targeting](https://substack.com/redirect/20ea308c-aac7-402a-89c6-3c5122143065?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the nearby Ali Al-Taher hill.

* Israeli forces also set fire to several homes and areas of land on the outskirts of Beit Yahoun.
* **Israel reaffirms plans to maintain occupation in parts of Lebanon, Gaza, and Syria:** Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz [said](https://substack.com/redirect/24fa1dfd-bedd-49df-8b96-57fff29bf166?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that Israel remains committed to maintaining its military presence in occupied areas of Gaza, southern Lebanon, and Syria, reaffirming the policy during an overnight call with U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth, the Jerusalem Post reported. Katz said Israeli forces would continue holding "security zones," calling the strategy a key lesson from October 7. "We have never asked the U.S. to act in our place along our borders. We are committed to protecting the residents of Israel from every threat, and that is what we intend to do," he said.

* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,250 killed, with 173,751 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,127 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,643, while 800 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Three Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Thursday:** Three Palestinians were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/16916832-17a1-43b3-97bb-30898cfd2d6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and several others wounded in separate Israeli attacks on Gaza City on Thursday morning, according to WAFA.

* In a separate airstrike, two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded after Israeli warplanes targeted the vicinity of Al-Sanafour Junction in the Al-Tuffah neighborhood.
* **Gaza government files complaint against UN official, says statement provided "pretext" for deadly Israeli strike: **Gaza's caretaker government [filed](https://substack.com/redirect/c4b6baa3-13f5-4a82-be78-aa7f94827c41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a formal complaint against UN Deputy Special Coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov, charging that a July statement fueled incitement against Palestinian police and preceded a deadly Israeli strike that killed eight officers.
* In a letter obtained by Drop Site, the government said Alakbarov's July 12 statement mischaracterized a police operation targeting alleged smuggling within a World Food Programme distribution site in Jabalia, despite a "direct and continuous coordination" with the UN.
* The complaint says Israeli forces struck a police post in Jabalia two days later, killing eight civil police officers, and argues that the UN statement "provided a pretext for incitement against government agencies and exposed their personnel to greater danger."
* Gaza's caretaker government, which is administrating the Strip following the recent dissolution of the Hamas-led government, called on the UN official to issue a clarification and reaffirm its commitment to resolving such matters through existing coordination channels.

* Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz [described](https://substack.com/redirect/8680f47a-231b-43aa-ae20-7a70fe01a8c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the plan as part of a "settlement revolution" in the occupied West Bank, saying the projects would support the long-term development of the settlements, according to the Times of Israel.
* **Colombia 's incoming government to restore full ties with Israel, open embassy in Jerusalem: **Colombia's incoming government under President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella will fully restore economic and diplomatic relations with Israel immediately after taking office on Aug. 7, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/2e345661-3108-4d65-9f89-b22634c3755f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday following talks in Washington with Colombia's foreign minister-designate, Omar Bula. Under a new bilateral roadmap, Colombia plans to open an embassy in occupied Jerusalem and begin efforts to eliminate mutual tourist visa requirements, reversing the policies of outgoing President Gustavo Petro.
* Petro severed diplomatic relations with Israel in May 2024, charging the Israeli government was committing genocide in Gaza, and later ordered the opening of a Colombian embassy in Ramallah, the seat of the Palestinian Authority in the occupied West Bank. He subsequently expelled the remaining Israeli diplomatic staff after Israeli forces intercepted the Global Sumud aid flotilla and abused participants, including Colombian activists.

* **Israel aid amendment fails, but House Democrats back cut:** An amendment to eliminate $3.3 billion in Israel funding from a State Department spending bill [failed](https://substack.com/redirect/e0431529-5ca6-4cab-aa16-18a48d7158e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 314-104 on Wednesday, but 103 Democrats voted to support it, more than half of those voting yes or no, with 98 against. Another ten voted present. Two years ago, just 37 Democrats voted to support a similar measure.
* Texas progressive Rep. **Greg Casar,** chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus,**** whipped Democratic support for the measure, proposed by Republican Rep.**Thomas Massie**(Ky.), writing in a letter to colleagues that the "American people are crying out for an end to U.S. tax dollars subsidizing Israel's military."

Pelosi and two other Democrats told colleagues privately on the floor that the Israeli treatment of Khanna in the West Bank played a role in their votes, according to a source familiar with the floor conversations. A Pelosi spokesperson didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
* Pelosi's support is especially surprising: at an Israeli lobbying conference seven years ago, she [argued](https://substack.com/redirect/a55b91ef-23e4-487a-b3b6-fd9ccf5453fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that even "if the Capitol crumbled to the ground, the one thing that would remain is our commitment" to U.S. aid to Israel.

She was just one of several Democrats who broke with AIPAC despite getting millions in support from them.
* Rep. **Rashida Tlaib**(Mich.)**,** whose principled objection to Israeli policy has often been solitary during her time in the House, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/eca124b2-75f0-4fd2-bde8-a5a4e23a0621?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) she was "proud" of colleagues who voted to stop funding Israel's genocide, urging people to remember the more than 73,000 Palestinians killed and millions made homeless. "Keep talking about Gaza. Never stop."
* **AIPAC,** [in a statement, ](https://substack.com/redirect/65f3105a-bad7-4c22-b60f-9eeee99c991c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)vowed to continue spending heavily to support members of Congress who back its agenda and oppose those who don't.
* Rep. **Thomas Massie,** in an interview this morning on [Breaking Points](https://substack.com/redirect/84dab87d-f453-4331-8caf-9ac4e23207d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), joined by his ally on the legislation,**** Rep. **Ro Khanna**(D-Calif.), said that Republican leadership allowed the vote to reach the floor because they wanted to produce chaos in Democratic Party ranks. * Washington exempted beef, coffee, rare earths, energy products, and aircraft. The tariffs are set to take effect on July 22.
* Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva called the move unjustified and said Brazil would pursue action through its Reciprocity Law and the World Trade Organization.
* **More than 500 feared dead after boats sink off Myanmar** : Two boats carrying more than 500 people, mostly Rohingya refugees, may have [capsized](https://substack.com/redirect/d3ab8c8f-f12e-4f62-bde5-c795c9a72d60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) off Myanmar's Rakhine and Irrawaddy coasts in recent days, the UN's refugee agency and International Organization for Migration said Thursday.
* The vessels left Rakhine State in late June.
* One lost contact shortly after departure, while the second, carrying about 280 people, is believed to have sunk off the Irrawaddy coast on July 8.
* Nearly 900 Rohingya refugees died or went missing in the Andaman Sea and Bay of Bengal last year, making the maritime route the world's deadliest for refugees, according to the UN.
* **Russian nuclear plant chief killed in drone strike** : Alexander Yakovlev, the chief engineer at Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, and his driver were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/c6b330fc-905d-4059-8bc2-a7e3d504059a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with his driver in a reported Ukrainian drone strike, the head of the Russian state nuclear corporation Rostatom said in a statement.
* The statement described the incident as a terrorist attack, adding that Yakovlev's killing was "an attack on the principle of nuclear facility safety."
* Yakovlev was responsible for overseeing technical and operational safety at Zaporizhzhia which is Europe's largest nuclear power plant.
* Rafael Grossi, the head of the International Atomic Energy Agency condemned the incident, stating that it "represents an unacceptable attack on the plant and its management, seriously threatening nuclear safety," while not attributing blame for the attack.
* **Protests in Kyiv after defense chief 's ouster:** Hundreds of protestors gathered in Kyiv after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy [dismissed](https://substack.com/redirect/ec2b166f-8d0d-452d-a89c-4c24767cda38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the country's Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.
* Fedorov had been credited with helping modernize Ukraine's drone capabilities and improving its battlefield performance during the conflict and his dismissal comes amid a broader shift in Zelenskyy's cabinet.
* Several Ukrainian senior officials and lawmakers resigned in protest over the decision, with deputy Air Force Commander Pavlo Yelizarov calling Fedorov's removal "a great evil for the country's defense capability" in a social media post announcing his resignation.
* **Ousted CHP leader Özel says new party in preparation**: Özgur Özel, the onetime leader of Turkey's primary opposition party, the Republican People's Party, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/67a47b80-7032-4fdd-9cb1-19d672a17378?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday that preparations are underway for a possible new political party, though any formal step would wait until legal proceedings over his ouster conclude.
* Özel said a decision could come by late July or early August if appeals against a court ruling that reinstated former leader Kemal Kilicdaroglu as chairman are blocked.
* **Recent militia massacres kill over 200 in Eastern Congo:** More than 200 civilians were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/efee59bc-be04-4710-9581-615f6e2c8e7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and hundreds more wounded, kidnapped, or forced into hiding between April and June across North Kivu in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, according to rights group BADILIKA, with M23 and ADF fighters primarily responsible for the death toll.
* The report also accuses other armed forces, including pro-government Wazalendo militias, of abductions, forced disappearances, arbitrary arrests, and widespread looting.
* M23, which has received backing from Rwanda, has seized large parts of mineral-rich eastern Congo, a major source of coltan and cobalt used in phones and electric vehicles.

Iran and Ceasefire U.S. hits Iran with fifth day of renewed attacks: U.S. forces two waves of strikes against Iran on Wednesday, targeting Iranian military capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz, the country's Central Command announced, with the earlier wave of strikes hitting Iran's Tunb Island. CENTCOM the second wave targeted military installations in the south and on the Persian Gulf coast, including Bandar Abbas. U.S. strikes hit Ahvaz in Iran's South, according to Iran's WANA. The U.S. launched multiple projectiles that landed in the vicinity of Shahid Baqaei Hospital, a hospital which specializes in the treatment of children with cancer. The hospital's director confirmed that 211 of its patients, including vulnerable children undergoing chemotherapy and those on ventilators, had to be urgently evacuated to nearby facilities like Golestan and Shafa hospitals. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei condemned the attack in a on X, calling it "barbaric" and a "cowardly war crime against the most innocent of human beings." U.S. strikes also hit sites in the north, with one hitting a storage facility near Semnan and the city's civilian airport, according to Al Jazeera. Other strikes were in Khondab, Andimeshk, Qeshm, Sirik, Konarak, Rask, and Chabahar. U.S. forces also fired missiles into the smokestack of a Curaçao-flagged oil tanker, the Belma, disabling it as it sailed toward Iran's Kharg Island, Central Command said Wednesday, the first commercial ship the U.S. has struck since its blockade resumed. CENTCOM also attempted to wave away the damage its strikes had already done to civilian infrastructure within the country, denying in a Thursday statement that it had targeted a civilian wheat storage facility in Hoveyzeh on Tuesday. Iran responds, hitting U.S. bases in the Gulf: Iran fresh missile and drone attacks on U.S. military sites in Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan early Thursday, hours after another round of American strikes on Iran. In Kuwait, Iran reported hitting radar systems, a Patriot air-defense battery, and fuel storage at the Ali al-Salem Air Base, according to state broadcaster IRIB. Kuwaiti officials reported engaging "hostile" attacks with at least 4 cruise missiles and 21 drones intercepted. Iran also said it struck U.S. facilities at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, where the Interior Ministry sounded air-raid sirens Thursday morning and urged residents to head to the nearest safe place. Jordan intercepted 8 Iranian missiles on Thursday, the state news agency Petra said. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it fired two waves of ballistic missiles at U.S. air bases in Jordan, claiming they had been used to launch strikes on Iran, including the attack near a children's cancer hospital. Kuwait's army also its air defenses were intercepting another wave of "hostile drone attacks" on Thursday. Iran calls Hormuz its "red line," vows devastating retaliation if U.S. hits infrastructure: Ibrahim Zolfaghari, a spokesman for Iran's Khatam Al-Anbiya Joint Headquarters, in a statement on Wednesday that "under no circumstances and in no way" would Iran permit America "to interfere in the Strait of Hormuz," calling this Iran's "unimpeachable red line." Zolfaghari added that Iran would pound the U.S.' Gulf allies "with steel blows" until "no trace" remains "as if" these countries "never existed from the beginning," should the U.S. carry out its threats against civilian infrastructure. This follows comments by President Donald Trump threatening to strike Iran's power plants and bridges next week unless Tehran returns to negotiations. "Next week it gets really bad for them," Trump told Fox News. "We're going to knock out all their power plants. We're going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate." Trump later said Iran "better behave" and told a defence summit that Tehran "wants to settle so badly," adding that Washington would decide whether to reach an agreement "or if we just finish it off." Iran told Vance Witkoff, Kushner were "abusing" their inside access to negotiations: During U.S.-Iran talks in Lake Lucerne, Switzerland, in late June, Iranian negotiators sent a private message to Vice President JD Vance through an intermediary warning that President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were undermining efforts to turn the June 17 framework into a lasting agreement, a senior Iranian official told Drop Site. According to the official, Iran accused the pair of exploiting insider knowledge of the negotiations for financial gain and raised concerns over leaks by Kushner to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The official added that Iran requested a share of what it estimated were $9 billion in profits from alleged market manipulation. The White House denied the claims, with spokesperson Anna Kelly saying no such message had been transmitted "to the United States," and accusing Drop Site of being "filled with hate for America." Read the full story by Jeremy Scahill and Ryan Grim. Watch the story. Pricey U.S. drone shot down: Another US MQ-9 drone, costing between $30-40 million, was on Thursday, Iran's Fars news agency reported, in Iran's southwest. In mid-May 2026 briefings to the Senate Armed Services Committee, defense officials testified that the active fleet of MQ-9 drones had dwindled significantly, plummeting to roughly 135 operational units, down from a baseline of 189 aircraft. The U.S. lost $1 billion worth of these drones in the first part of the war, according to their testimony. Araghchi goes to Doha: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to Doha on Thursday to "meet Qatari officials and to express his condolences" to Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani following the death of Qatar's former emir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, according to Araghchi's official Telegram channel. The visit may also be a sign that diplomatic channels remain open through Qatar, a key mediator in U.S.-Iran talks. Pakistan, another key mediator, said Thursday it remains committed to the memorandum reached last month despite the collapse of the initial pause in hostilities. "While the implementation of the MOU is facing challenges," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said, "Pakistan will continue to encourage all sides to end violence and resume technical-level talks." WSJ: Trump favors expanding military operations against Iran : Trump is leaning toward expanding U.S. military operations against Iran after briefings from top aides, including options to seize Kharg Island and bomb the fortified Pickaxe Mountain site, U.S. officials the Wall Street Journal. Trump is also considering airstrikes against civilian energy infrastructure, according to the report. Lebanon Israeli ceasefire violations continue across southern Lebanon: Israeli forces carried out a series of airstrikes and artillery attacks across southern Lebanon on Thursday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. In the Nabatieh district, Israeli warplanes two airstrikes on the outskirts of the Al-Deir neighborhood in Nabatieh al-Fawqa at around 2 p.m., followed about 45 minutes later by a drone strike the nearby Ali Al-Taher hill. Israeli warplanes the outskirts of Baraachit and Beit Yahoun at dawn, while Israeli artillery shelled the town of Rshaf in the Tyre (Sour) district. Israeli forces also set fire to several homes and areas of land on the outskirts of Beit Yahoun. Israel reaffirms plans to maintain occupation in parts of Lebanon, Gaza, and Syria: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz on Thursday that Israel remains committed to maintaining its military presence in occupied areas of Gaza, southern Lebanon, and Syria, reaffirming the policy during an overnight call with U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth, the Jerusalem Post reported. Katz said Israeli forces would continue holding "security zones," calling the strategy a key lesson from October 7. "We have never asked the U.S. to act in our place along our borders. We are committed to protecting the residents of Israel from every threat, and that is what we intend to do," he said. Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, four Palestinians were killed, one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks, and 28 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,250 killed, with 173,751 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,127 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,643, while 800 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Three Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Thursday: Three Palestinians were and several others wounded in separate Israeli attacks on Gaza City on Thursday morning, according to WAFA. One person was killed and three others injured in Israeli artillery shelling in the Al-Zeitoun neighborhood. In a separate airstrike, two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded after Israeli warplanes targeted the vicinity of Al-Sanafour Junction in the Al-Tuffah neighborhood. Gaza government files complaint against UN official, says statement provided "pretext" for deadly Israeli strike: Gaza's caretaker government a formal complaint against UN Deputy Special Coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov, charging that a July statement fueled incitement against Palestinian police and preceded a deadly Israeli strike that killed eight officers. In a letter obtained by Drop Site, the government said Alakbarov's July 12 statement mischaracterized a police operation targeting alleged smuggling within a World Food Programme distribution site in Jabalia, despite a "direct and continuous coordination" with the UN. The complaint says Israeli forces struck a police post in Jabalia two days later, killing eight civil police officers, and argues that the UN statement "provided a pretext for incitement against government agencies and exposed their personnel to greater danger." Gaza's caretaker government, which is administrating the Strip following the recent dissolution of the Hamas-led government, called on the UN official to issue a clarification and reaffirm its commitment to resolving such matters through existing coordination channels. Israel approves $330 million to expand road network for West Bank settlements : The Israeli government a budget late Wednesday allocating 1.075 billion shekels (about $330 million) over three years for road construction serving dozens of illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank, a proposal initially submitted by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, WAFA reported. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz the plan as part of a "settlement revolution" in the occupied West Bank, saying the projects would support the long-term development of the settlements, according to the Times of Israel. Colombia 's incoming government to restore full ties with Israel, open embassy in Jerusalem: Colombia's incoming government under President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella will fully restore economic and diplomatic relations with Israel immediately after taking office on Aug. 7, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar on Wednesday following talks in Washington with Colombia's foreign minister-designate, Omar Bula. Under a new bilateral roadmap, Colombia plans to open an embassy in occupied Jerusalem and begin efforts to eliminate mutual tourist visa requirements, reversing the policies of outgoing President Gustavo Petro. Petro severed diplomatic relations with Israel in May 2024, charging the Israeli government was committing genocide in Gaza, and later ordered the opening of a Colombian embassy in Ramallah, the seat of the Palestinian Authority in the occupied West Bank. He subsequently expelled the remaining Israeli diplomatic staff after Israeli forces intercepted the Global Sumud aid flotilla and abused participants, including Colombian activists. U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Israel aid amendment fails, but House Democrats back cut: An amendment to eliminate $3.3 billion in Israel funding from a State Department spending bill 314-104 on Wednesday, but 103 Democrats voted to support it, more than half of those voting yes or no, with 98 against. Another ten voted present. Two years ago, just 37 Democrats voted to support a similar measure. Texas progressive Rep. Greg Casar, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, whipped Democratic support for the measure, proposed by Republican Rep.Thomas Massie(Ky.), writing in a letter to colleagues that the "American people are crying out for an end to U.S. tax dollars subsidizing Israel's military." Former Speaker Nancy Pelosi and** Rep.Katherine Clark(Mass.), the House's second-ranking Democrat, both voted in favor of the bill, with the former saying about her vote that there is "a real sense that the status quo cannot continue." Pelosi and two other Democrats told colleagues privately on the floor that the Israeli treatment of Khanna in the West Bank played a role in their votes, according to a source familiar with the floor conversations. A Pelosi spokesperson didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Pelosi's support is especially surprising: at an Israeli lobbying conference seven years ago, she that even "if the Capitol crumbled to the ground, the one thing that would remain is our commitment" to U.S. aid to Israel. Rep. Pat Ryan(N.Y.), a more hawkish Democrat and an AIPAC ally in the past, also voted in favor of the bill and announced afterward that he would return his donations to AIPAC, calling donations to Israel "wrong on every level." Rep. Sarah Elfreth, who won her seat in Maryland in 2024 thanks to millions in support from AIPAC, voted present, dragging the U.S. into war with Iran. She was just one of several Democrats who broke with AIPAC despite getting millions in support from them. Rep. Rashida Tlaib(Mich.), whose principled objection to Israeli policy has often been solitary during her time in the House, she was "proud" of colleagues who voted to stop funding Israel's genocide, urging people to remember the more than 73,000 Palestinians killed and millions made homeless. "Keep talking about Gaza. Never stop." AIPAC, to continue spending heavily to support members of Congress who back its agenda and oppose those who don't. Rep. Thomas Massie, in an interview this morning on , joined by his ally on the legislation, Rep. Ro Khanna(D-Calif.), said that Republican leadership allowed the vote to reach the floor because they wanted to produce chaos in Democratic Party ranks. He also ruled out running in a special election to replace Kentucky Republican Mitch McConnell , if McConnell dies, saying that opposition from Trump and AIPAC is too steep a hill to climb. Massie and Khanna also teamed up to pass legislation releasing the Epstein files. Groups sue Trump administration over ICC sanctions Democracy for the Arab World Now and the Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide a lawsuit Tuesday in federal court in Manhattan arguing that Trump administration sanctions on the International Criminal Court violate the U.S. First Amendment, claiming that the State Department's targeting of ICC officials inhibits Americans from Constitutionally protected political action, fearing that they will be exposed to the same fate if they try to work with the Court. "The Trump administration is using the blunt instrument of economic sanctions not only to punish human rights defenders but to police the political expression of millions of Americans," said Omar Shakir , executive director of DAWN. The suit names President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio as defendants. Pentagon weighs Cuba military options as Iran war resumes: U.S. military planners have options for possible action against Cuba, CBS News reported on Wednesday, including an Army-led air assault by the 101st Airborne Division. Officials, who convened in late June to discuss the contingencies of such a mission (including its sequencing, logistical considerations, and other risks), said that action remains unlikely, given the shifting of resources towards the U.S.'s current war in Iran. Two officials also relayed to the office that War Secretary Pete Hegseth has been a more aggressive proponent of action against Cuba, and that Joint Chiefs Chairman Dan Caine has voiced reservations about such a policy, with the former reportedly responding to Trump's dissatisfaction with being informed about the potential limits of military action. House GOP unveils budget to fund Iran war: House Republican leaders a budget blueprint Wednesday that would use the reconciliation process to unlock up to $95 billion, including $73 billion for military operations in Iran and $12 billion for farmers. Republicans have also attempted to attach the voting restrictions proposed under the SAVE Act, which Democrats have consistently voted down, to the bill. Budget Committee Chairman Jodey Arrington (R-Texas) set a Thursday committee vote, though Democrats and some Republicans, including Rep. Warren Davidson(Ohio), have raised objections that could complicate the bill's path through reconciliation rules. Report finds widespread abuse allegations at Texas ICE facility: An 84-page report Wednesday by Human Rights Watch and the American Civil Liberties Union found that 64 of 71 detainees interviewed at Camp East Montana, a facility at Fort Bliss in El Paso, said they were beaten by guards or witnessed beatings, alongside accounts of denied medical care and filthy conditions. In March, ICE removed the facility's operator, who had won the right to build and manage the camp even though it had no experience running an ICE detention facility. The change came as 49 deficiencies at East Montana were documented in an internal ICE review. Venezuelan man becomes 22nd ICE detainee to die this year : Jes us Manuel Arenas-Silva, a 45-year-old Venezuelan man, Monday of suspected cardiac arrest while being transferred between Georgia detention facilities, ICE said, marking the 22nd death in the agency's custody this year, The Guardian reported. Arenas-Silva, who was arrested last Thursday, was denied medication for an existing condition, according to his family. Vance admits administration mishandled Epstein files release : Vice President JD Vance told podcast host Joe Rogan in an interview released Wednesday that the Trump administration "screwed up the comms" on releasing files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein , saying they should have been released from the start. Vance said former Attorney General Pam Bondi "overstated" what the administration had after she said an alleged Epstein "client list" was on her desk, adding he didn't believe the missteps were an attempt to hide anything. Vance also Epstein's "clear" connections to the "highest levels" of both American and Israeli intelligence services. Other International News Sheinbaum rejects DEA claim of cartel ties to Mexican government: Mexican** President Claudia Sheinbaum on Wednesday that recent remarks by DEA Administrator Terry Cole were "baseless and unfortunate." A day earlier, Cole called the Mexican government and drug cartel networks "one in the same," Reuters reported, and called these ties the agency's "number one priority." Sheinbaum said the DEA should instead focus on drug trafficking and money laundering within the United States, which Sheinbaum called the world's largest market for illegal drugs. U.S. imposes 25% tariffs on Brazil, exempts key exports : The Trump administration late Wednesday 25% duties on many Brazilian imports following over 30 rounds of failed negotiations, Reuters reported. Washington exempted beef, coffee, rare earths, energy products, and aircraft. The tariffs are set to take effect on July 22. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva called the move unjustified and said Brazil would pursue action through its Reciprocity Law and the World Trade Organization. More than 500 feared dead after boats sink off Myanmar : Two boats carrying more than 500 people, mostly Rohingya refugees, may have off Myanmar's Rakhine and Irrawaddy coasts in recent days, the UN's refugee agency and International Organization for Migration said Thursday. The vessels left Rakhine State in late June. One lost contact shortly after departure, while the second, carrying about 280 people, is believed to have sunk off the Irrawaddy coast on July 8. Nearly 900 Rohingya refugees died or went missing in the Andaman Sea and Bay of Bengal last year, making the maritime route the world's deadliest for refugees, according to the UN. Russian nuclear plant chief killed in drone strike : Alexander Yakovlev, the chief engineer at Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, and his driver were with his driver in a reported Ukrainian drone strike, the head of the Russian state nuclear corporation Rostatom said in a statement. The statement described the incident as a terrorist attack, adding that Yakovlev's killing was "an attack on the principle of nuclear facility safety." Yakovlev was responsible for overseeing technical and operational safety at Zaporizhzhia which is Europe's largest nuclear power plant. Rafael Grossi, the head of the International Atomic Energy Agency condemned the incident, stating that it "represents an unacceptable attack on the plant and its management, seriously threatening nuclear safety," while not attributing blame for the attack. Protests in Kyiv after defense chief 's ouster: Hundreds of protestors gathered in Kyiv after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy the country's Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Fedorov had been credited with helping modernize Ukraine's drone capabilities and improving its battlefield performance during the conflict and his dismissal comes amid a broader shift in Zelenskyy's cabinet. Several Ukrainian senior officials and lawmakers resigned in protest over the decision, with deputy Air Force Commander Pavlo Yelizarov calling Fedorov's removal "a great evil for the country's defense capability" in a social media post announcing his resignation. Ousted CHP leader Özel says new party in preparation: Özgur Özel, the onetime leader of Turkey's primary opposition party, the Republican People's Party, Wednesday that preparations are underway for a possible new political party, though any formal step would wait until legal proceedings over his ouster conclude. Özel said a decision could come by late July or early August if appeals against a court ruling that reinstated former leader Kemal Kilicdaroglu as chairman are blocked. Recent militia massacres kill over 200 in Eastern Congo: More than 200 civilians were and hundreds more wounded, kidnapped, or forced into hiding between April and June across North Kivu in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, according to rights group BADILIKA, with M23 and ADF fighters primarily responsible for the death toll. The report also accuses other armed forces, including pro-government Wazalendo militias, of abductions, forced disappearances, arbitrary arrests, and widespread looting. M23, which has received backing from Rwanda, has seized large parts of mineral-rich eastern Congo, a major source of coltan and cobalt used in phones and electric vehicles. This is how I’ve lived my whole life, and how I’ll lead as governor.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I want to tell you a little about how this campaign actually operates — because it says a lot about how I’ll lead as governor.
**I’ve never believed in wasting money.**
That’s not a campaign talking point; it’s how I’ve lived my _whole_ life. When you grow up watching every dollar, you learn quickly that money represents someone’s time, sacrifice, and trust.
That mindset shapes every decision we make.
We’re building a campaign powered by people, not billionaires.
We focus on what helps us win: organizing communities, talking directly with voters, and showing up everywhere — not just where it’s convenient.
Sometimes that means long drives instead of flights. El Paso to Austin? No problem. It means reusing placards after events, meeting in libraries or community centers instead of expensive venues. Most of all, it means knowing we’re accountable for how we spend what supporters like you give.
I know how much a contribution can mean — especially right now. When someone decides to give, that’s an act of trust. I don’t take that lightly for a second.
**[Peter, if you’re able to pitch in $5 today, you’ll be helping us keep building a campaign that’s disciplined, people-powered, and strong enough to defeat Greg Abbott.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260716_1_thrift.Bx_tii&refcode=em20260716-1581&amount=5&t=1&akid=1581%2E299639%2E-HM0pD)**

I’m asking you to have my back for whatever they throw our way.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2360%2E791427%2EQqA6Dz)
Friend, yesterday the House of Representatives voted on a measure that would cut $3.3 billion in annual U.S. military aid to Israel.
**I voted YES to cut that funding.**
Over the last three years we have watched in horror as Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, invaded Lebanon, and allowed settler violence to flourish in the West Bank. But this violence didn’t start three years ago — for decades, Palestinians have been subjected to a brutal and illegal occupation without basic human rights.
Through all of the war crimes and violations of international law that have stacked up, American taxpayers have paid for it with their hard-earned money. **It’s unconscionable.**
Not only would blocking this aid bring that money home, but it would put diplomatic pressure on Israel to change course. Rather than supporting Israel no-questions-asked, the United States can and should be leading the charge on pressuring Israel to end the violence, end the apartheid, end the occupation, and get serious about a Palestinian state. Ending US aid is the first critical step of that process.
Friend, while this measure did not pass, 104 members, including 103 Democrats, voted "yes" alongside me. **This represents the largest coalition in support of blocking aid to Israel in the history of the House.** The pressure our movement has put on both the Democratic and Republican parties is working.
But here’s the problem: When you stand up for human rights, peace, and the dignity of Palestinians, the well-funded Israel lobby will do everything they can to defeat you.
AIPAC and its allies have already spent **_hundreds of millions of dollars_** this election cycle, with the express goal of beating pro-Palestine progressives like myself.
I have been a top target of the pro-Israel lobby, Trump, and all of MAGA for years now. I don’t know what comes next, but I’m asking you to have my back for whatever they throw our way.
[**Please, if you believe that it’s far past time to cut off aid to Israel and fight for justice and self-determination for Palestine, donate to my campaign. clean_body: I’m asking you to have my back for whatever they throw our way. Friend, yesterday the House of Representatives voted on a measure that would cut $3.3 billion in annual U.S. military aid to Israel. I voted YES to cut that funding. Over the last three years we have watched in horror as Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, invaded Lebanon, and allowed settler violence to flourish in the West Bank. But this violence didn’t start three years ago — for decades, Palestinians have been subjected to a brutal and illegal occupation without basic human rights. Through all of the war crimes and violations of international law that have stacked up, American taxpayers have paid for it with their hard-earned money. It’s unconscionable. Not only would blocking this aid bring that money home, but it would put diplomatic pressure on Israel to change course. Rather than supporting Israel no-questions-asked, the United States can and should be leading the charge on pressuring Israel to end the violence, end the apartheid, end the occupation, and get serious about a Palestinian state. Ending US aid is the first critical step of that process. Friend, while this measure did not pass, 104 members, including 103 Democrats, voted "yes" alongside me. This represents the largest coalition in support of blocking aid to Israel in the history of the House. The pressure our movement has put on both the Democratic and Republican parties is working. But here’s the problem: When you stand up for human rights, peace, and the dignity of Palestinians, the well-funded Israel lobby will do everything they can to defeat you. AIPAC and its allies have already spent hundreds of millions of dollars this election cycle, with the express goal of beating pro-Palestine progressives like myself. I have been a top target of the pro-Israel lobby, Trump, and all of MAGA for years now. I don’t know what comes next, but I’m asking you to have my back for whatever they throw our way. # _Our Weekly Newsletter Is Here!_
---
| | **Hello everyone!****What a fantastic week it's been! Elizabeth and the campaign team have been all across the district, meeting voters, sharing ideas, and having a lot of fun along the way.****We kicked off the week with a virtual Healthcare Town Hall, where Elizabeth discussed her plans to protect Medicare and Medicaid, expand access to affordable healthcare, and answered thoughtful questions from community members.****On Friday, Elizabeth enjoyed spending time with neighbors at the Mechanicsville Tomato Festival, one of the district’s favorite summer traditions. On Saturday, Elizabeth attended barbecues with both the Gloucester and New Kent Democrats, and participated in a Veterans Roundtable with two fellow VA-01 candidates. She spoke about her military service and how it continues to inspire her commitment to serving the community.****We wrapped up the weekend on Sunday with a successful pool party and postcard-writing event, followed by a great candidate talk with the Hanover Democrats. Then on Monday, Elizabeth continued the momentum by meeting with the Henrico Democrats.****Thank you to everyone who joined us, volunteered, and cheered us on throughout the week. Your support keeps this campaign moving forward, and we can't wait to see you at our next event!**

Friend,

This summer, my kids have spent a lot of time on the campaign trail. They knocked on doors, met neighbors, handed out stickers, and learned that democracy isn't something that just happens. It's something we all help build.
But we still make lots of other memories, and there is nothing better than getting out on the water with the fam—whether that’s a pool, Lake Saint Clair, or even just the sprinkler in the back yard.
Watching those little splashes spread across the water got me thinking that's how campaigns work, too. One conversation becomes another. One volunteer inspires a friend. One donation helps us knock on another hundred doors. Before long, those small ripples grow into something that reaches every corner of our community.
Three kids. Three weeks until the primary. A $3 donation today would help us make every one of those days count. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cbh_email-26q3?refcode=x_260716_jumpingin_act&amount=3]

* **00:13:55** -- We unpack J.D. Vance's Joe Rogan appearance, the Epstein fallout, and why calling it a "messaging problem" completely misses the point.
* **00:19:02** -- A bigger conversation about why both parties too often hide behind messaging instead of solving the real problems people are facing.
* **00:23:21** -- We wrap up with some lighter moments, college football, family stories, and why sometimes you need a laugh after talking about democracy all morning.

clean_body: Democratic women are ready to protect our elections. | = Peter, Donald Trump wants everyone watching Georgia tonight. In a prime-time address, Trump is expected to cite “newly declassified intelligence” to revive his false and dangerous claims about Georgia’s 2020 election. While Trump once again tries to rewrite the results of a free and fair election and undermine Georgians’ faith in their votes, we want to make sure you know about someone else in Georgia. = | = Trump has made his strategy clear: spread lies about elections when he doesn't like the outcome, intimidate officials who uphold the results, and push for greater federal control over how Americans vote. That is exactly why electing Democratic pro-choice women governors is so important. Governors oversee the systems that keep elections safe, secure, and accessible. They can stand up to federal overreach, protect election officials from political intimidation, and make sure that every eligible voter has the opportunity to cast a ballot and have it counted. **VIRGINIA HAS OFFICIALLY REJOINED RGGI** On July 1, Virginia rejoined the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, more commonly known as RGGI. Virginia's participation in RGGI will drive down pollution from power plants and provide hundreds of millions of dollars each year to help protect communities from flooding and to fund energy efficiency programs that lower bills. And by reducing our dependence on coal and methane gas, participating in RGGI will help protect consumers from high fuel costs.

**8 SWVA SCHOOL-BASED HEALTH CLINICS CLOSING DUE TO FEDERAL CUTS** Clinics in Southwest Virginia are closing. Washington is costing rural Virginians basic medical care and mental health services, and pushing the clinics left standing beyond their limits. Congress should be fighting to strengthen these services, not allowing them to disappear. Contact your federal representative: (202) 224-3121.

We've already seen where this leads: federal investigations targeting Georgia's elections, attacks on election officials, and a relentless effort to undermine faith in our democracy.

Dear Patriot,
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)When I started undercover investigative journalism as a college student at Rutgers, I pored over the history of journalism. I studied the techniques of great authors who broke stories that transformed America. From Stetson Kennedy, who infiltrated the highest echelons of the KKK in the 1940s, to Upton Sinclair, who went undercover in the 1900s working in a meatpacking plant in Chicago. Sinclair's book, The Jungle, resulted in a national uproar over food safety and the creation of what is now the Food and Drug Administration. Every notable author and journalist who came before me used similar tactics to get the story: fearless boots on the ground. And as I've found in my nearly 20 years as a journalist, my job is limited to what I can see and record through public access . . . undercover or not. At the end of each investigation, I'm left wanting more. I can see the threads dangling in front of me, waiting to be pulled, but accessible only to law enforcement and their powers to investigate. **But today, the world has shifted . . .** This morning, I testified before the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee (HSGAC) of the United States Senate regarding "Fraud in America." Following my opening remarks, where I expressed my limits as a journalist, something extraordinary happened. **Committee Chairman Rand Paul invited me to submit requests for subpoenas to his office.** Notably, Senator Paul, as the chairman of HSGAC, is the only member of the Senate with **unilateral authority** to issue subpoenas. From Upton Sinclair to Woodward and Bernstein, the model for action has been: **Journalist publishes → Institution reacts.** After my testimony before the Senate, that model will be inverted . . . **at least temporarily.** Power shifts. Rules change. **Doors close.** That's why we have to [**move fast**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.), and I need your help more than ever to take advantage of an unprecedented offer. I'm putting together a small team of researchers who can pull those dangling threads left from current and previously closed investigations.
* We can follow the money trails to see who is truly behind the fraudulent ballots.
* We have a shot at unraveling the global web of money that funds illegal immigration.
* We finally have a chance to see the documents behind Pfizer's illegal "Gain of Function" research on COVID-19.

**At the bottom of every rabbit hole is a lock box filled with receipts.** Senator Paul just handed us a golden key. [**Will you help me fund this new squad?**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) Remember, Al Capone was brought down by an accountant. In today's dollars, Capone's criminal enterprise was worth $2 billion. Taxpayers are being defrauded of at least **$250 billion every year** on the federal level alone — money out of your pocket, counted against your vote. And at the Senate hearing on Fraud in America, our elected officials admitted that the governmental bodies tasked with stopping fraud for decades are wholly ineffective. That leaves us to do the job. Are you in? [**Help me and my team get to work.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) We have HUNDREDS of Al Capones to take down who have been ripping all of us off and stealing our national treasure . . . and our votes. **Time is short.**[**Please help me and my team get started today.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) Thank you for all that you do.
In Truth,James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group
P.S. I'm still grasping the impact of the Senate hearing. Most journalists might just smile and say "thank you" if Senator Paul asked them to submit subpoena requests to him. But those journalists have not gone as deep as I have. They haven't risked their lives. Some never leave the comfort of their office. I know what the offer means. I've lived with the frustration of knowing that the true players behind an operation can hide in darkness. With your help, OMG is taking advantage of this immediately — until the door closes. [**Please help fund this rapid response team today.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

Hi, it’s Nancy Pelosi.
I've spent my career fighting For The People — and building the Democratic power it takes to win those fights. Today, I’m asking for your help.
I've seen leaders come and go. I've watched some rise to the moment and others shrink from it. And after all these years, I can tell you that I know a fighter when I see one.
Raja Krishnamoorthi is a fighter.
As Speaker of the House, I appointed Raja, my dear friend and extraordinary colleague, to the Intelligence Committee, where he helped to keep our country safe and helped lead the impeachment of Donald Trump. I also appointed Raja to the Special Select Oversight Subcommittee responsible for taking on price-gouging pharmaceutical companies, investigating COVID scams and lowering healthcare costs. I worked with Raja for a decade in standing up to Big Tobacco, the gun lobby and many others who prioritize profit over our children’s health and safety.
And I watched Raja face down hatred and bigotry that would have broken a lesser person — and come back stronger every single time.
So when Raja told me he was launching Equal Opportunity Now — a new group dedicated to finding and supporting the next generation of Democratic leaders and priorities — I didn't hesitate. This is exactly what this moment demands.
Because let me be clear about what we are facing:
Donald Trump and his MAGA extremists are a danger to our Constitution, our children and our Democracy. Full stop.
They are actively working to dismantle the institutions that are the foundation of our government of, by and For The People. They are stripping away the safety net that millions of working families depend on to give massive tax breaks to their ultra rich MAGA donors on the backs of vulnerable Americans. And they are counting on us to be too tired, too divided or too discouraged to stop them.
They don't know us very well, do they? We don’t agonize — we organize!
I have spent decades building the Democratic infrastructure it takes to win — to take back the House, to protect our majorities and to deliver For the People. That is the ongoing work of my PAC to the Future. And Raja is building the bench of bold, battle-tested leaders who will carry this fight forward for decades to come with Equal Opportunity Now.
Today, I’m asking you to support Raja’s Equal Opportunity Now and my PAC to the Future. We need both as we build an America that honors the vision of our Founders, the service and sacrifice of our men and women in uniform and the dreams and aspirations of our children.
Will you split a donation of $25 or $50 between PAC to the Future and Equal Opportunity Now right now? Your support will do directly to winning the fights ahead. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-pac2thefuture]

SPLIT A DONATION NOW! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-pac2thefuture]
I could not be more proud of Raja’s leadership and of continuing to fight alongside him for our shared values and for our Democracy. Let's get to work!
NANCY
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

body:
Trump’s speech tonight reminds us that the stakes of the midterm election couldn’t be higher.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=7764%2E582294%2E1ugp4t)
Chris Pappas here.
Tonight Donald Trump will address the country and is expected to once again revisit the 2020 election, repeating the same false claims that have already been rejected over and over again.
He's trying to undermine confidence in Georgia's elected leaders, including Jon Ossoff, who is on the ballot for re-election this fall.
This is a familiar pattern: While families are focused on affording their bills and building a better future, Donald Trump continues to focus on settling old political scores and using his office to serve himself.
**This is a dangerous reminder of why the upcoming election matters so much.[If you already understand the stakes and are on board with flipping the Senate blue, please split a donation between our campaign in New Hampshire and Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia right away »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260716_2._Ve5JN&refcode=em20260716-2&t=2&akid=7764%2E582294%2E1ugp4t)**
Public service is about putting the people you represent first, standing up for what’s right, and making sure our government is accountable to the people it serves.
That’s the work I’ve done for New Hampshire in Congress, and it’s the work I’ll continue to do in the Senate.
We need a Senate that can serve as a check on Donald Trump’s authoritarian agenda and make clear that no one is above the law.
**But we can only have that if we keep New Hampshire and Georgia blue.** Jon Ossoff is facing off against a Republican candidate who has embraced Donald Trump’s false claims about the 2020 election.
And here in New Hampshire, national Republicans have made clear this open seat is one of their top targets because they know what’s at stake.
If Republicans maintain control of the Senate, Donald Trump and his allies will have more opportunities to evade accountability and put politics ahead of the people.
I’ve spent my career fighting for stronger ethics rules, greater transparency, and a government that works for the people – not the powerful interests.
So I’m asking you today: **[Will you split a $5 contribution between Jon Ossoff and my campaign today? Together we can protect these critical Senate seats and build the majority we need to put a check on Donald Trump’s abuse of power.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260716_2._Ve5JN&refcode=em20260716-2&t=3&akid=7764%2E582294%2E1ugp4t)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260716_2._Ve5JN&amount=5&refcode=em20260716-2&t=22&akid=7764%2E582294%2E1ugp4t)**
Trump’s speech tonight reminds us that the stakes of the midterm election couldn’t be higher.
I’m running to make sure our Senate holds those in power accountable – not one that looks the other way.
**[Chip in $5 or whatever you can today, split between my campaign and Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia, to flip the Senate, fight back against far-right extremism, and defend our democracy.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260716_2._Ve5JN&refcode=em20260716-2&t=23&akid=7764%2E582294%2E1ugp4t)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260716_2._Ve5JN&amount=5&refcode=em20260716-2&t=24&akid=7764%2E582294%2E1ugp4t)**
Thank you,
Chris
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_footer?refcode=em20260716-2&t=25&refcode2=7764_582294_1ugp4t&akid=7764%2E582294%2E1ugp4t)**

Speaker Johnson says he’s a Christian. I say he’s the Antichrist.
Senator Rafael Warnock called out Mike Johnson for his hypocrisy out loud. He said he couldn’t understand why the Speaker could read the bible, say a prayer, and then cut a trillion dollars out of Medicaid — calling it waste, fraud, and abuse.
My grandmother taught me in Sunday school that we are supposed to treat every single person that we meet with dignity.
Speaker Mike Johnson? He wants to take healthcare away from millions of Americans. There’s nothing Christian about him.
Mike Johnson thinks that he can hide behind his faith — but I know the truth.

name: Free Speech Daily Sponsor
subject: Is the UN about to seize 400,000 acres of American soil?
body:
The only thing standing between the UN’s 400,000-acre power grab and American soil is one decision.
---
| | | | | |
---
| | | | | [View in browser](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAci1ymdzOA-B3cPmCxOPith-moYmYLaQJxCp7NXN58xVuoe9b30w6BMP8ufDIpWgLXMmrsdmMH0FrFUqRiSV-fkWzrebpAY5mK4O9qZr "View in Browser")
---
_**A Special Message from our Sponsor**_ _Please note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of_ _Free Speech Daily_ _and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily_ _._
---
| *|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | | | [ ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAci1ymd0SLL3BRbixb0VCYB4AbENmUKegECc3z_VSkZP6MxvGT078Z92EpR3KrZ6_al2axlWTyJhq-nF2eC4Ab7vVFf1irFhbo7tDR8Z)
---
| | Dear Fellow Patriot,

On July 19, a committee of 21 foreign governments gavels into session in Busan, South Korea – and somewhere in the days that follow, they’ll decide whether a 400,000-acre stretch of Georgia answers to them.

Not to Georgia. Not to America.

To _them_ – the United Nations.

And don’t kid yourself that it stops at one swamp. Hand the UN 400,000 acres of Georgia and you’ve handed them the precedent – the next piece of America comes easier, and the one after that easier still.

I’m Craig Rucker, President of CFACT – the Committee for a Constructive Tomorrow – and I want to give you a frank update on what the United Nations is actually up to right now.

Last weekend, you and I were lighting fireworks for America’s 250th birthday – a quarter of a millennium since a handful of farmers and shopkeepers told the most powerful empire on earth to take its crown and its tax collectors and pound sand.

**And now, before the smoke clears, the UN’s culture bureaucrats want to plant their flag in the Okefenokee Swamp.**

They don’t call it a flag, of course. They call it a “World Heritage Site” – a designation of “outstanding universal value.” (Translation: it’s not really yours anymore.)

The UN swears it would “only monitor” this swath of American land. (Right – the way a fox “only monitors” the henhouse.) Ask the folks in Charlton, Ware, and Clinch counties in Georgia what “monitor” means.

They’re the ones who’d wake up to find their hunting land, their timber, their own backyards redrawn as a “buffer zone” to “protect” a swamp that’s been doing just fine on its own since before there was a United Nations to mismanage it.

No hunting. No logging. No pulling weeds. No say. That’s the “universal value” on offer.

[**Will you please add your name to CFACT’s Declaration of Independence from the UN to tell President Trump and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to pull this nomination off the table before the July 19 deadline**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAci1ymd1JCmxiU558LHeS68xiD7JYAImJJ2H7b_evLHHHBui3yn6tRcPVu7Nj4HpSPOKZt6S4zYcnYmrgVOOPn7_XAc5v_kmoK1dI8y9)?
[**Add My Name to the Declaration >>**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAci1ymd2aoZ2CX3gyFXjIxAOPMJcN_w9MhG1W07yicla9kdMYRXdotlTxIMvLyUCuOuHWplSZb_wQHKROyHuOGiz2bk4QMXBcTceppFE)
So how did we get here? A midnight gift in January 2025.

The Okefenokee sat on a UN “tentative list” for some 40 years, going nowhere – until the Biden administration, just before clearing out its desks, rammed through the nomination without so much as a phone call to the people who actually live there.

**A parting gift to the UN – from the same crew that spent four years handing out pieces of American sovereignty to anyone who asked.**

And the outfit advising the UN on whether to bless it?

The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) – the global green bureaucracy whose own network brags about cramming climate “education” into the Paris accord that Trump already tore up.

This was never about alligators and peat moss. **It’s about handing a chunk of America to the climate agenda’s permanent government – the one nobody elected and nobody can fire.**

President Trump already walked America out of UNESCO – one of 66 international outfits he’s shown the door to, including the UN’s climate convention itself. Good.

But walking out of UNESCO alone doesn’t stop this.

**The nomination rides a separate track, and the United States is still bound to the “World Heritage Convention.”**

Which means unless Secretary Burgum formally rescinds it, those 21 foreign governments get the final word on American soil – whether we’re members of their little club or not.

One signature stands between the UN and the Okefenokee – Secretary Burgum’s, on an order pulling this nomination off the table. _That’s the whole fight, in a single stroke of a pen_.

This is exactly the fight CFACT was built for.

Our team went to Folkston, Georgia – cameras rolling – and sat down with the county commissioners the UN never bothered to consult, and put their warnings on the record while the national press looked the other way.

**We’re also one of the only conservative outfits holding official NGO observer status at the United Nations – which means when they convene, we have the standing to be in the room and fight them to their faces.**

That’s the difference between a think tank and a DO tank. And because we don’t take one dime of taxpayer money, there isn’t a globalist on this earth who can buy us off or shut us up.

_The good news?_ This fight is winnable, and the momentum is ours.

Three counties have already passed ordinances against it. When the UN’s own advisors held their little meeting down in Folkston, it did not go the way they planned.

America has walked away from UNESCO before – under Reagan, and again under Trump. The pattern is hard to miss: when Americans actually show up, the globalists lose.

So let’s show up.

[**Add your name to the Declaration today – and then chip in $25, $50, or $100 to keep CFACT’s boots on the ground for the next land grab, because there is always a next one**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAci1ymd3XxjnsP91H70LfQP9aLujQbZqcrdiNO1bANH2ipnnt6-PNmAklpmrK4kXReDMpas-52IP1zxyMZTlXTm3ZX-BXCj6NEEjMfZY).

Two hundred and fifty years ago, we declared our independence from a faraway power that thought it owned us.

It’s time to do it again.

For American sovereignty,

Craig Rucker
President

P.S. – Twenty-one foreign governments are about to vote on a piece of Georgia, fifteen days after we celebrate 250 years of telling distant powers exactly where to put their opinions about our land. [**Add your name before July 19 – and let’s make this Independence Day mean something**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5Mzl9AAwAAAAAAci1ymd4EG0hCB5rigZ9EAZerNua1XAS7ANSJWGBhVWrytr4ml4fCYpQsENy8TGIs_CNo0Py5GhkBR5V37ne6M0ONLI4A3baJ4mAODCl).
