Protesters rat a rally organized by staff and students of Sana'a University against recent airstrikes on Sana'a airport on July 15, 2026. Photo by Mohammed HUWAIS / AFP via Getty Images.
A leading official from Yemen's Ansarallah vowed that the group would block Saudi access to the Bab al-Mandab strait--a vital bottleneck connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean--in response to strikes on Sana'a airport on Monday that were blamed on Saudi Arabia. The move would exacerbate the economic impact of the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz, particularly on Asian markets currently relying on Saudi crude exports through the Red Sea.
Ansarallah claimed on Monday night to have launched retaliatory strikes with ballistic missiles and drones hitting Abha airport in Saudi Arabia. But the Ansarallah official, Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, told Drop Site News that the strikes were "merely one of the initial steps in a broader escalation...we will focus on intensifying our military operations," adding that "the Bab al-Mandab strait is a legitimate leverage tool."
Ansarallah leader Abdulmalek al-Houthi added to the threats in a [speech](https://substack.com/redirect/22dbb6fd-c1bf-4d9b-91c6-7a757e8f56b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday, saying that "all Saudi oil facilities and vital installations" were targets.
A [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/4ec92125-b873-4f5f-8e7b-67bbeef952ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also supported Ansarallah's pledge, warning that other oil and gas export routes, in addition to the Strait of Hormuz, could be closed to the U.S. and its allies.
It remained unclear whether Ansarallah would in fact carry out the threat to close off the vital waterway to Saudi Arabia, yet the latest developments have ushered in a dangerous game of brinkmanship.
The strikes on Sana'a airport were the first attack by Saudi Arabia against Ansarallah, also known as the Houthis, since 2022. The attack and retaliatory missile and drone launches by the Houthis into Saudi Arabia, along with the vows of further escalation, threaten to upend a four-year-long tenuous ceasefire just as the truce between the U.S. and Iran is crumbling over access through the Strait of Hormuz.
The Saudi-backed, internationally recognized Yemeni government, largely based in Riyadh, [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/617d297b-0b21-4438-94d2-ea2a11f7476e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) responsibility for the [strikes](https://substack.com/redirect/4b5e026f-a110-4d0c-b21e-e91652605099?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sana'a airport on Monday saying they aimed to prevent the landing of an inbound Iranian [flight](https://substack.com/redirect/99d9cb9c-51cf-4601-9538-f77fa45cd4d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) carrying an Ansarallah delegation returning from Tehran for the funeral of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei who was assassinated by a U.S.-Israeli strike in March.
At least four individual strikes hit the runway shortly after a UN humanitarian air service flight departed from Sana'a. The Iranian Mahan Air passenger plane diverted and later landed safely at Ansarallah-controlled Hodeidah airport on Yemen's Red Sea coast.
In response, Ansarallah's military spokesman Yahya Saree accused Saudi Arabia of being behind the strikes and [declared](https://substack.com/redirect/a25b31ec-6655-4c0d-9d9e-00e163af1ea5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the attack "ended the de-escalation phase," threatening "consequences." The reported strikes claimed by Ansarallah on Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, around 100 kilometers from Yemen's northern border, soon followed. Flights to and from Abha were [cancelled](https://substack.com/redirect/5d027850-0324-4d9f-a2f7-baae1d9ed299?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) late Monday and Tuesday morning.
The initial strikes on Sana'a airport came amid mounting tension and warnings from the Yemeni government after the first Mahan Air aircraft landed in Sana'a on July 3 to take the Ansarallah delegation to Iran. Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council (PLC) called the flight "a clear violation" of Yemen's sovereignty. Saudi warplanes attempted to prevent the flight from reaching Sana'a, according to a video statement by Saree who warned that Ansarallah would target Saudi "airports and vital interests on land and sea" if they violated Ansarallah airspace.
No commercial flights have left Sana'a since Israeli strikes [destroyed](https://substack.com/redirect/43260da4-d490-41e9-89e3-84635396fc2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Yemenia Airways' sole Airbus A330 and three smaller A320 passenger planes in May 2025. A further Israeli strike three-weeks later destroyed the single remaining Yemenia A320 operating from Sana'a after it had returned from Jordan. Ansarallah was [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/fc5bbab3-c94c-42d8-b194-ca743e0bf0c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of [seizing](https://substack.com/redirect/c99bedbf-23e5-4e54-8ccf-85b20f2fd640?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four of the five destroyed Yemenia Airways planes in July 2024, leaving the national airline with just two aircraft in operation for the rest of the country.
Rhetoric had been heating up between the two sides over the planned return of the Ansarallah officials. The Yemeni government [insisted](https://substack.com/redirect/8777cc14-e280-4d69-a348-9174718060e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the use of a Yemenia Airways plane rather than Iran's Mahan Air, which they said would set a precedent for opening a Tehran-Sana'a air bridge facilitating transport of weapons, components and IRGC military officials to Ansarallah-controlled territory.
The PLC[ claim](https://substack.com/redirect/8777cc14-e280-4d69-a348-9174718060e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Ansarallah rejected an initiative proposed earlier in the month to restart Yemenia Airways civilian flights from Sana'a to Jordan. In a [video](https://substack.com/redirect/de9788f5-a084-4d97-abe9-7dc1aff3aab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) statement following this week's strikes, Yemen's President Dr. Rashad Mohammed al-Alimi affirmed, "not a single Iranian aircraft will return to our lands, starting today."
Al-Bukhaiti, who is a member of Ansarallah's politburo, was onboard the Mahan flight along with more than 200 passengers. He told Drop Site that the continued Saudi blockade and resulting humanitarian impact meant the Bab al-Mandab strait is "a legitimate leverage tool to enforce a 'blockade-for-blockade' equation." A measure, he said, that would only target countries participating "in the aggression against Yemen."
"We will focus on intensifying our military operations to enforce a 'blockade-for-blockade' equation, compelling Saudi Arabia to stop intercepting civilian flights to and from Yemen--since it understands only the language of force," al-Bukhaiti warned, underscoring the pledge to block the maritime choke point between Yemen and the Horn of Africa to Saudi traffic.
Around 25% of global container trade usually passes through the Bab al-Mandab strait and north to the Suez Canal. The alternative route around South Africa's Cape of Good Hope [adds](https://substack.com/redirect/dcc17efa-32a5-457d-98aa-21219196d92b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) between 10-14 days onto the voyage from Asia to Europe and approximately $1 million in extra fuel costs per round-trip.
The impact of any Red Sea obstruction in response to this week's strikes would be far more acute than before the U.S. and Israel launched their war against Iran. Since March, Saudi Arabia has become reliant on its East-West oil pipeline to circumvent the Strait of Hormuz and export crude heading to Asia via its west coast terminal at Yanbu and south through the Bab al-Mandab strait. More than 80% of crude oil and LNG normally transiting through the Strait of Hormuz is bound for Asian countries including India, China, and Japan.

Yemen's war began in 2014 when Ansarallah fought their way south from their northern homeland of Sa'ada, seizing control of the capital in September of that year. Six months later, in March 2015, as Ansarallah continued to push south, then-President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi escaped Ansarallah house arrest and fled to Riyadh. Soon afterwards, Saudi Arabia launched an air war backed by the U.S. with the United Arab Emirates as its main partner against Ansarallah.
The seven years of bombing that followed killed over 8,900 civilians, while a Saudi blockade, combined with Ansarallah siege tactics and aid appropriation, resulted in an [estimated 85,000 children](https://substack.com/redirect/573c1b5c-1cc3-4ae3-ac6b-eb3e9e674428?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) under the age of five dying from hunger in less than four years, and airstrikes[ contributing](https://substack.com/redirect/b0b6d4aa-02ac-414f-af92-66a4b1cff2fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the world's worst cholera [outbreak](https://substack.com/redirect/b0b6d4aa-02ac-414f-af92-66a4b1cff2fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in modern history. A ceasefire was reached in March 2022 and has largely held since. Monday's strikes marked the first significant escalation in more than four years.
President Donald Trump and the U.S. State Department reportedly [gave](https://substack.com/redirect/4ca0144e-e9cd-45b7-a8ce-458c60ca86ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their[ support](https://substack.com/redirect/9888d3a1-6006-4a00-a29e-c486307a5352?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the Saudi strikes on Monday. Although the kingdom has not publicly claimed responsibility, the Yemeni military lacks the capability to carry out airstrikes and lost its air force and aging fighter jets to Ansarallah more than a decade ago. The fighter jets were subsequently destroyed by Saudi airstrikes in 2015.
Ansarallah has played an increasingly important role in the Iran-led Axis of Resistance in recent years. In response to Israel's genocide in Gaza, Ansarallah hijacked an Israeli-owned car carrier in the Red Sea in November 2023 and launched multiple attacks on commercial vessels, effectively shuttering the southern Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab strait from November 2023 to late 2024. Numerous rounds of Ansarallah ballistic missiles and drones also targeted Israel.
The attacks on commercial shipping were countered by regular U.S. and U.K strikes against Ansarallah for more than a year while U.S., U.K. and European warships came under heavy attack from Ansarallah drone swarms and anti-ship ballistic missiles. Israel joined the fight in July 2024 with their own air and naval strikes.
Two months into his second term in office Trump launched Operation Rough Rider,__ a new, much more intensive daily bombing campaign supported by the U.K that killed at least 238 civilians in 340 strikes over 53 days. Saudi Arabia is now the fourth nation to bomb Ansarallah in the past 18 months.
But Ansarallah involvement in the ongoing conflict between the U.S. and Iran has been more muted with missiles and drones launched at Israel on just two occasions, in April and June. A June 8 announcement by Saree declaring the closing of the Bab al-Mandab strait to Israel has not resulted in attacks on commercial vessels as seen in 2024.
While escalation against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea or a return to all-out war is possible, Mohammed al-Basha, a longtime Yemen analyst and founder of the U.S.-based risk advisory Basha Report, said it's unlikely.
"At this stage, the exchange appears to have been a calculated tit-for-tat operation designed to send political and military messages," al-Basha told Drop Site. "An important indicator is that Saudi Arabia still allowed the Iranian Mahan Air flight to land at Hodeidah airport. That decision suggests Riyadh deliberately left room for negotiations rather than choosing full escalation," he added.
A Red Sea blockade on Saudi Arabia that Al-Bukhaiti warned of would put considerable strain on such measured responses. As the U.S.-Iran ceasefire continues to unravel, Tehran has now [reportedly](https://substack.com/redirect/8d3b2aad-ad68-4bfb-b28b-2c79d0897608?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) called on Ansarallah to be prepared to close the strait in the event the U.S. carries out strikes targeting Iran's power infrastructure.

Photo by Mohammed HUWAIS / AFP via Getty Images. A leading official from Yemen's Ansarallah vowed that the group would block Saudi access to the Bab al-Mandab strait--a vital bottleneck connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean--in response to strikes on Sana'a airport on Monday that were blamed on Saudi Arabia. The move would exacerbate the economic impact of the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz, particularly on Asian markets currently relying on Saudi crude exports through the Red Sea. Ansarallah claimed on Monday night to have launched retaliatory strikes with ballistic missiles and drones hitting Abha airport in Saudi Arabia. But the Ansarallah official, Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, told Drop Site News that the strikes were "merely one of the initial steps in a broader escalation...we will focus on intensifying our military operations," adding that "the Bab al-Mandab strait is a legitimate leverage tool." Ansarallah leader Abdulmalek al-Houthi added to the threats in a on Thursday, saying that "all Saudi oil facilities and vital installations" were targets. A on Wednesday by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also supported Ansarallah's pledge, warning that other oil and gas export routes, in addition to the Strait of Hormuz, could be closed to the U.S. and its allies. It remained unclear whether Ansarallah would in fact carry out the threat to close off the vital waterway to Saudi Arabia, yet the latest developments have ushered in a dangerous game of brinkmanship. The strikes on Sana'a airport were the first attack by Saudi Arabia against Ansarallah, also known as the Houthis, since 2022. The attack and retaliatory missile and drone launches by the Houthis into Saudi Arabia, along with the vows of further escalation, threaten to upend a four-year-long tenuous ceasefire just as the truce between the U.S. and Iran is crumbling over access through the Strait of Hormuz. The Saudi-backed, internationally recognized Yemeni government, largely based in Riyadh, responsibility for the on Sana'a airport on Monday saying they aimed to prevent the landing of an inbound Iranian carrying an Ansarallah delegation returning from Tehran for the funeral of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei who was assassinated by a U.S.-Israeli strike in March. At least four individual strikes hit the runway shortly after a UN humanitarian air service flight departed from Sana'a. The Iranian Mahan Air passenger plane diverted and later landed safely at Ansarallah-controlled Hodeidah airport on Yemen's Red Sea coast. In response, Ansarallah's military spokesman Yahya Saree accused Saudi Arabia of being behind the strikes and that the attack "ended the de-escalation phase," threatening "consequences." The reported strikes claimed by Ansarallah on Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, around 100 kilometers from Yemen's northern border, soon followed. Flights to and from Abha were late Monday and Tuesday morning. The initial strikes on Sana'a airport came amid mounting tension and warnings from the Yemeni government after the first Mahan Air aircraft landed in Sana'a on July 3 to take the Ansarallah delegation to Iran. Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council (PLC) called the flight "a clear violation" of Yemen's sovereignty. Saudi warplanes attempted to prevent the flight from reaching Sana'a, according to a video statement by Saree who warned that Ansarallah would target Saudi "airports and vital interests on land and sea" if they violated Ansarallah airspace. No commercial flights have left Sana'a since Israeli strikes Yemenia Airways' sole Airbus A330 and three smaller A320 passenger planes in May 2025. A further Israeli strike three-weeks later destroyed the single remaining Yemenia A320 operating from Sana'a after it had returned from Jordan. Ansarallah was of four of the five destroyed Yemenia Airways planes in July 2024, leaving the national airline with just two aircraft in operation for the rest of the country. Rhetoric had been heating up between the two sides over the planned return of the Ansarallah officials. The Yemeni government on the use of a Yemenia Airways plane rather than Iran's Mahan Air, which they said would set a precedent for opening a Tehran-Sana'a air bridge facilitating transport of weapons, components and IRGC military officials to Ansarallah-controlled territory. The PLC Ansarallah rejected an initiative proposed earlier in the month to restart Yemenia Airways civilian flights from Sana'a to Jordan. In a statement following this week's strikes, Yemen's President Dr. Rashad Mohammed al-Alimi affirmed, "not a single Iranian aircraft will return to our lands, starting today." Al-Bukhaiti, who is a member of Ansarallah's politburo, was onboard the Mahan flight along with more than 200 passengers. He told Drop Site that the continued Saudi blockade and resulting humanitarian impact meant the Bab al-Mandab strait is "a legitimate leverage tool to enforce a 'blockade-for-blockade' equation." A measure, he said, that would only target countries participating "in the aggression against Yemen." "We will focus on intensifying our military operations to enforce a 'blockade-for-blockade' equation, compelling Saudi Arabia to stop intercepting civilian flights to and from Yemen--since it understands only the language of force," al-Bukhaiti warned, underscoring the pledge to block the maritime choke point between Yemen and the Horn of Africa to Saudi traffic. Around 25% of global container trade usually passes through the Bab al-Mandab strait and north to the Suez Canal. The alternative route around South Africa's Cape of Good Hope between 10-14 days onto the voyage from Asia to Europe and approximately $1 million in extra fuel costs per round-trip. The impact of any Red Sea obstruction in response to this week's strikes would be far more acute than before the U.S. and Israel launched their war against Iran. Since March, Saudi Arabia has become reliant on its East-West oil pipeline to circumvent the Strait of Hormuz and export crude heading to Asia via its west coast terminal at Yanbu and south through the Bab al-Mandab strait. More than 80% of crude oil and LNG normally transiting through the Strait of Hormuz is bound for Asian countries including India, China, and Japan. Drop Site News is reader-supported. Consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Yemen's war began in 2014 when Ansarallah fought their way south from their northern homeland of Sa'ada, seizing control of the capital in September of that year. Six months later, in March 2015, as Ansarallah continued to push south, then-President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi escaped Ansarallah house arrest and fled to Riyadh. Soon afterwards, Saudi Arabia launched an air war backed by the U.S. with the United Arab Emirates as its main partner against Ansarallah. The seven years of bombing that followed killed over 8,900 civilians, while a Saudi blockade, combined with Ansarallah siege tactics and aid appropriation, resulted in an under the age of five dying from hunger in less than four years, and airstrikes to the world's worst cholera in modern history. A ceasefire was reached in March 2022 and has largely held since. Monday's strikes marked the first significant escalation in more than four years. President Donald Trump and the U.S. State Department reportedly their for the Saudi strikes on Monday. Although the kingdom has not publicly claimed responsibility, the Yemeni military lacks the capability to carry out airstrikes and lost its air force and aging fighter jets to Ansarallah more than a decade ago. The fighter jets were subsequently destroyed by Saudi airstrikes in 2015. Ansarallah has played an increasingly important role in the Iran-led Axis of Resistance in recent years. In response to Israel's genocide in Gaza, Ansarallah hijacked an Israeli-owned car carrier in the Red Sea in November 2023 and launched multiple attacks on commercial vessels, effectively shuttering the southern Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab strait from November 2023 to late 2024. Numerous rounds of Ansarallah ballistic missiles and drones also targeted Israel. The attacks on commercial shipping were countered by regular U.S. and U.K strikes against Ansarallah for more than a year while U.S., U.K. and European warships came under heavy attack from Ansarallah drone swarms and anti-ship ballistic missiles. Israel joined the fight in July 2024 with their own air and naval strikes. Two months into his second term in office Trump launched Operation Rough Rider, a new, much more intensive daily bombing campaign supported by the U.K that killed at least 238 civilians in 340 strikes over 53 days. Saudi Arabia is now the fourth nation to bomb Ansarallah in the past 18 months. But Ansarallah involvement in the ongoing conflict between the U.S. and Iran has been more muted with missiles and drones launched at Israel on just two occasions, in April and June. A June 8 announcement by Saree declaring the closing of the Bab al-Mandab strait to Israel has not resulted in attacks on commercial vessels as seen in 2024. While escalation against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea or a return to all-out war is possible, Mohammed al-Basha, a longtime Yemen analyst and founder of the U.S.-based risk advisory Basha Report, said it's unlikely. "At this stage, the exchange appears to have been a calculated tit-for-tat operation designed to send political and military messages," al-Basha told Drop Site. "An important indicator is that Saudi Arabia still allowed the Iranian Mahan Air flight to land at Hodeidah airport. That decision suggests Riyadh deliberately left room for negotiations rather than choosing full escalation," he added. A Red Sea blockade on Saudi Arabia that Al-Bukhaiti warned of would put considerable strain on such measured responses. As the U.S.-Iran ceasefire continues to unravel, Tehran has now called on Ansarallah to be prepared to close the strait in the event the U.S. carries out strikes targeting Iran's power infrastructure. | A guest post by| . subject: The race for TN-09
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Justice Democrats
body:
Justin has never backed down from a fight — and he won’t start now.
#
Peter,
With **three weeks left** until the Tennessee primary, we need to pull out all the stops to help Justice Democrat Justin J. Pearson win and advance to the general election.
This race changed _overnight_ after long-time establishment incumbent Rep. Steve Cohen dropped out following the Tennessee GOP gerrymandering the last Black district in TN out of existence.
**Now, Justin has emerged as the frontrunner.** And winning this primary means he’ll face the _full weight_ of the Tennessee Republican machine — politicians hell-bent on drowning out Black and working-class voters’ voices and delivering another seat to Donald Trump and his MAGA allies.
**[But Justin has never backed down in the face of any challenge — and he won’t start now, Peter. Rush a split donation to his campaign and Justice Democrats now to make sure he has the resources to WIN >>](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260716-1-jp.pIEqZF&refcode=em20260716-38034&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=2&akid=38034%2E1203867%2El9pViW)**
**[Contribute ››](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260716-1-jp.pIEqZF&refcode=em20260716-38034&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=3&akid=38034%2E1203867%2El9pViW)**
Justin is running because he knows that the way things stand isn’t serving working people. He knows that our government has been corrupted by the billionaires, corporate lobbyists, and Do-Nothing politicians who protect wealthy interests while working families struggle to get by.
As a state representative and member of the Tennessee Three, Justin is the definition of a fighter. He’s ready to go to Washington to achieve **Medicare for All, a higher minimum wage, a ban on AI data centers, environmental and climate justice, and an economy that works for everyday people.**
Like every Justice Democrat, he refuses to take a single cent from corporate PACs or AIPAC. His campaign is powered by grassroots supporters who believe it’s time to replace establishment Democrats and Republicans with leaders willing to _actually_ fight for them.
**Progressive power is growing across the country, and this final primary race in TN-09 is our chance to keep building on that momentum through November.**
**[With just three weeks left, we need to expend every resource to reach as many voters as possible with Justin’s message before the August 6th primary. Can you pitch in any amount to his campaign and Justice Democrats today to help send another unapologetic progressive champion to Congress?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260716-1-jp.pIEqZF&refcode=em20260716-38034&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=4&akid=38034%2E1203867%2El9pViW)**

In solidarity,
Justice Democrats

body:
Letters to the editor and signs can make a difference for a candidate. | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/4174954b975a/traveling-towards-victory-varnam-travels-the-state-11032542?e=326fe9326d)

| | | I am not slowing down. My family and I spent our weekends in parades and talking with Wisconsinites.

Wisconsinites are ready for change and leaders they can count on to stand strong when things get tough. I am the only former elected official that has a proven record of standing up for residents and taxpayers. I have earned the trust and endorsements from Wisconsin Family Action PAC and Pro-Life Wisconsin Victory Fund PAC to lead Wisconsin as Lieutenant Governor.

In order to be on the ballot in November and support Tom Tiffany, I need your help to turn out the vote on August 11th. One easy way to submit a letter to the editor to your local newspaper. A candidate does better in a community when a support letter is published in the local paper.

A letter to the editor can be simple. If you don't know what to write about, below are a few highlights about myself:
* The only candidate who was a former local elected official as the Mayor of Lancaster. When David completed his third term, Lancaster had the lowest property taxes and utility fees of any city in Grant County.
* David Varnam is the only statewide candidate from Western Wisconsin. He will be an advocate for our rural communities and restore the faith, family-centered values that built Wisconsin.
* Varnam will be bold on lowering taxes, protect the unborn, keep men out of women’s sports and their bathrooms, work to deport criminal illegal aliens, and give parents a choice and a voice in education.
* Varnam is a former federal policy analyst at Focus on the Family for Dr. James Dobson.
* Varnam is endorsed by Pro-Life Wisconsin Victory Fund PAC and Wisconsin Family Action PAC.
* Vote David Varnam for Republican Lieutenant Governor on August 11th.

Will you help me win in August and submit a letter to the editor this week?

If you need help submitting a letter, please let me know.

With Gratitude,

David Varnam
Candidate for Lieutenant Governor

# [Trump scores massive win as Buffett endorses his Fed chair pick](https://substack.com/redirect/71b985cf-b4f6-437e-b366-5800a7ecd369?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Warren Buffett described President Trump's selection of Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve chair **[as a good choice noting the new leader's focus on two percent inflation](https://substack.com/redirect/9e0b86dc-ed64-45bc-9680-a4a883357693?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9e0b86dc-ed64-45bc-9680-a4a883357693?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and maximum employment.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1ae39fe0-e740-44be-87a8-eddaaa2e290f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Good Choice for Tough Job** : Buffett said Warsh will do the best he can at achieving the assigned job of hitting inflation and employment goals.
* **Rates Held Steady Initially** : Warsh presided over holding interest rates steady in his first meeting as chair in June.
* **Cares About the Country** : Buffett praised that Warsh cares about the country like many others despite tough decisions.
* **Testimony This Week** : The new Fed chair is returning to Capitol Hill for Senate Banking Committee testimony on Wednesday.

# [Senator Rounds hails Warsh's rock-solid stance on inflation control](https://substack.com/redirect/f79dd65f-b5b9-4d7f-b891-6fb6f1e5ab1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Senate Banking Committee member Mike Rounds said Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh **[struck the right tone on inflation control and central bank independence](https://substack.com/redirect/74d50d9a-70e1-4ad8-bc51-1a9f4ec9d800?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/74d50d9a-70e1-4ad8-bc51-1a9f4ec9d800?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)during recent congressional testimony.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f79dd65f-b5b9-4d7f-b891-6fb6f1e5ab1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Focus on Inflation Control** : Rounds noted Warsh started by emphasizing the need to get inflation under control aligning with congressional efforts.
* **Rates Maintained in June** : The senator said the Fed was correct to maintain interest rates during Warsh's first meeting as chair.
* **Independence Important** : Rounds stressed wanting the Federal Reserve to make decisions based on what they believe is right.
* **Lower Mortgage Rates Desired** : Long term goal includes bringing down thirty year mortgage rates but requires getting inflation down first.

* * *
* * *
# [IRS chief urges every American family to get Trump Accounts](https://substack.com/redirect/f79dd65f-b5b9-4d7f-b891-6fb6f1e5ab1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
IRS CEO Frank Bisignano urged enrollment of every family in Trump Accounts, the tax-deferred child investment vehicles, **[aiming for all 70 million children under 18 with 6.5](https://substack.com/redirect/f366c0b6-a81e-40e8-83c8-7c1237355944?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/f366c0b6-a81e-40e8-83c8-7c1237355944?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)million already signed up.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f79dd65f-b5b9-4d7f-b891-6fb6f1e5ab1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Universal Enrollment Goal** : Bisignano said the objective is to have 70 million children under 18 with Trump Accounts and every family enrolled.
* **Technology Driven Process** : He described it as a technology business and plans simple enrollment through tax preparers and banks.
* **Incentives Spur Uptake** : Financial incentives include $1,000 federal seed money for 2025-2028 babies, employer matches and philanthropist grants.
* **Expansion Leadership Task** : Bisignano has been tapped to lead the Trump Accounts expansion while also heading Social Security.

* * *
* * *
# [Trump strikes back hard demanding reversal of New York data ban](https://substack.com/redirect/f79dd65f-b5b9-4d7f-b891-6fb6f1e5ab1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Donald Trump **[slammed New York Gov. Kathy Hochul's moratorium on large AI data centers,](https://substack.com/redirect/4585997d-5984-4e06-97d9-410d0e267308?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** calling it a terrible decision and demanding the state change policy immediately for job growth.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/330c8c42-0f08-4211-95be-11a61cf78375?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Data Centers Job Driver** : Described as one of the biggest driving forces in future jobs and money machines for states where built.
* **Moratorium Called Terrible** : Executive order bars construction of data centers using 50 or more megawatts for up to one year.
* **Public Backlash Growing** : Concerns over fresh water use, power consumption and rising utility prices amid AI infrastructure boom.
* **Payment Mandate Pushed** : Data centers must pay for their own water and power with leftovers benefiting state and local communities.

New York Fed President John Williams stated i**[nflation has peaked with rates well positioned to bring it down](https://substack.com/redirect/2e1e91f9-7284-4d53-b994-f964104417ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** citing five encouraging reasons and easing drivers like oil and tariffs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f79dd65f-b5b9-4d7f-b891-6fb6f1e5ab1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Decline to Three Point Two Five** : Williams expects overall inflation to fall to around three point two five percent by year end then glide to two percent goal.
* **Easing Key Drivers Noted** : Oil prices likely peaked post Iran conflict, tariffs no significant additional impulse, AI imbalances receding with more supply.
* **Solid Economy and Labor** : Growth solid on trend labor market stable with well anchored inflation expectations.
* **June CPI Sharp Drop** : Consumer prices posted unexpected zero point four percent drop in June bringing annual rate to three point five percent.

# [Apple Goldman and Chevron ignite massive July Dow rally](https://substack.com/redirect/f79dd65f-b5b9-4d7f-b891-6fb6f1e5ab1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Apple Goldman Sachs and Chevron are leading the Dow Jones Industrial Average in July with 8 to 12% gains each, fueled by unrelated drivers in technology, banking and energy sectors.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f79dd65f-b5b9-4d7f-b891-6fb6f1e5ab1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Apple Valuation Surge** : The stock added over half a trillion dollars nearing $5 trillion valuation and hitting multiple records.
* **Goldman Post Earnings Rally** : Broke above June record after earnings rising over 150% from April low with high price weight influence.
* **Chevron Energy Rebound** : Rebounded from 20% percent loss as energy sector recovery challenging technical moving averages.
* **Concentrated Tech Strength** : Megacap rebound continues but technology sector remains July's weakest showing concentrated leadership.

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | U.S. GOVERNMENT DIGITAL DOLLAR PLAN We have urgent news... name: Mike (Molly's husband)
subject: What you may not know about my wife, Molly.
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/MG%20LOGO%20-WEB%20%281%29.png]
Peter,
If you have an ICE OUT sign on your lawn, or give a nod to the houses that do, then my wife, Molly Gray, is your candidate for Vermont Lt. Governor.
The heartbreaking news out of Texas and Maine this last week shows us we can't let up on our efforts to keep our communities and our state safe, and for ALL Vermonters. ICE killed two immigrants in the last week — people who were working for and contributing to their communities.
Molly said it best earlier this week: “Texans deserve answers, Mainers deserve answers, Vermonters and all Americans deserve answers. We want ICE out of our communities, and we want a full investigation, to know the results and we want accountability”.
But Molly doesn’t just make statements, she’s done the work. No other candidate in the race has dedicated themselves to serving, advocating for, and deeply caring about our new Vermont neighbors as she has. And before you write me off as biased (which I am), consider this:
I’ve watched Molly lie awake at night, trying to figure out how to keep the Vermont Afghan Alliance — the statewide organization she helped build from the ground up — from crumbling amid the dumpster fire of Elon Musk's DOGE.
I've waited with our son Jack for Molly to return home from Northwest Regional Correctional Facility, after working around the clock to help prevent an Afghan man wrongfully detained by ICE from being moved to an out-of-state detention facility, and ultimately back to Afghanistan.
I've seen Molly keep her phone on all night, knowing a family member of a Vermonter lost in Trump's cruel immigration system and held in an ICE facility in Louisiana might call, and knowing she could connect him with an immigration attorney.
I watched Molly walk out the door at 9 pm on March 11 — the night of the Dorset Street debacle — to attend the South Burlington Police Department press conference. Why? She felt a duty to understand why it happened, and to assist immigration attorneys and advocates in making sure those who were unlawfully detained had support.
This is real. This is get-your-hands-dirty work. This is pushing back against Trump. This isn't a political strategy to win a campaign. This is my wife, Molly Gray, showing up for the community during an incredibly challenging time.
I'm lucky to have Molly by my side, and I'm proud of her. She doesn't just talk about standing up for Vermonters, she shows up, again and again, when it’s hard and when no one’s watching. body:
Josh Shapiro failed to lead. Pennsylvania still brought home "Best in Show" because others stepped up.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/gc9vH9RyZWc?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | | Peter —
When Josh Shapiro decided Pennsylvania would not participate in the Great American State Fair he didn’t just make a political statement.
He let down Pennsylvania businesses, farmers, artisans, and workers who deserved the opportunity to showcase everything that makes our Commonwealth exceptional.
But fortunately, the story doesn’t end there.
Instead of accepting defeat, Senators Dave McCormick and John Fetterman put politics aside and worked together to ensure Pennsylvania was represented.
Thanks to their bipartisan leadership, Pennsylvania not only had a presence at the Fair...
**We won best in show!**
That outcome says everything.
When leaders lead, Pennsylvania wins.
When politicians play politics, Pennsylvanians lose.
Stacy Garrity saw that firsthand.
On the very first day of the Fair - before Pennsylvania’s booth was even opened - Stacy traveled to the fair to support Pennsylvania businesses and see what our Commonwealth was missing because of Shapiro’s failure to lead.
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | Pennsylvania should never have been in a position where two U.S. Senators had to step in to clean up a problem the Governor created.
But they did.
And because Dave McCormick and John Fetterman chose cooperation over partisanship, Pennsylvania received the recognition it deserved.
That’s the kind of leadership Pennsylvanians expect.
It’s also a reminder that putting Pennsylvania first isn’t about party labels.
It’s about showing up, working together, and doing what’s right for the Commonwealth.
Josh Shapiro failed that test.
Pennsylvania passed it anyway.
\- Team Garrity

clean_body: Josh Shapiro failed to lead. Pennsylvania still brought home "Best in Show" because others stepped up. | | | | | | | | | | | Peter — When Josh Shapiro decided Pennsylvania would not participate in the Great American State Fair he didn’t just make a political statement. He let down Pennsylvania businesses, farmers, artisans, and workers who deserved the opportunity to showcase everything that makes our Commonwealth exceptional. But fortunately, the story doesn’t end there. Instead of accepting defeat, Senators Dave McCormick and John Fetterman put politics aside and worked together to ensure Pennsylvania was represented. Thanks to their bipartisan leadership, Pennsylvania not only had a presence at the Fair... We won best in show! That outcome says everything. When leaders lead, Pennsylvania wins. When politicians play politics, Pennsylvanians lose. Stacy Garrity saw that firsthand. On the very first day of the Fair - before Pennsylvania’s booth was even opened - Stacy traveled to the fair to support Pennsylvania businesses and see what our Commonwealth was missing because of Shapiro’s failure to lead. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Pennsylvania should never have been in a position where two U.S. Senators had to step in to clean up a problem the Governor created. But they did. And because Dave McCormick and John Fetterman chose cooperation over partisanship, Pennsylvania received the recognition it deserved. That’s the kind of leadership Pennsylvanians expect. It’s also a reminder that putting Pennsylvania first isn’t about party labels. It’s about showing up, working together, and doing what’s right for the Commonwealth. Josh Shapiro failed that test. Pennsylvania passed it anyway. \- Team Garrity | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Paid for by Garrity for PA 4075 Linglestown Rd PMB 119 Harrisburg, PA 17112-1020 * USA or |

Dear Fellow American, President Trump's efforts have helped purge "wokeism" from our military, federal government, and elsewhere. Many supporters tell me they feel like commonsense Americans can finally declare "victory" over the radical left's woke agenda. **Unfortunately, they couldn 't be more wrong....** Liberal politicians--and even Democratic Socialists--are still threatening to spread the woke agenda across the country. That's why _I 'm writing today to remind you that **Judicial Watch** is continuing to fight this woke agenda at the state and local level, where it is still prominent_. In fact, I have a **HUGE update** to share from Evanston, Illinois, where Judicial Watch is prosecuting a **historic class-action lawsuit** against the city's **race-based reparations** law that is handing out **_$20 million taxpayer dollars to blacks only_. ** You read that right. **This is one of the most important lawsuits in Judicial Watch 's 32-year history...** | [HELP US DEFEAT THE WOKE AGENDA ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84156&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)
This reparation scheme clearly **_violates_** the U.S. Constitution's guarantee for **_equal protection_** to all by **_discriminating_** against everyone who does not identify as black. And now, President Trump's **_Department of Justice (DOJ)_**_has filed a motion to join our historic fight for equal protection_. | [JOIN OUR FIGHT FOR EQUAL PROTECTION ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84156&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)

Josh Shapiro can't hide behind the Governor's office forever.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/gkW8_4tsJ5p?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | | Peter,
For years, Josh Shapiro has acted as though the powers of the Governor’s Office exist to serve his personal interests.
Last week, a federal judge reminded him that they don’t.
In a lawsuit involving a property dispute at Josh Shapiro’s private residence, **the court ruled that Shapiro cannot simply shield himself behind the office he holds.**
The lawsuit centers on a dispute over a strip of land next to Josh Shapiro’s private residence. After negotiations with his neighbors fell apart, the dispute ended up in federal court. Shapiro tried to hide behind the office of Governor, but the court made clear that he will have to answer for his actions as a private homeowner.
This case was never about the Governor’s Office.
It was about Josh Shapiro’s personal property.
The rules should apply equally to everyone.
Whether you’re Governor of Pennsylvania or a homeowner on any street in the Commonwealth, accountability matters.
Pennsylvanians deserve leaders who respect both the law and public trust, not politicians who seem to believe the rules are different for them.

# [Jim Clyburn's endorsement means the world to me](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=205768308&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA1NzY4MzA4LCJpYXQiOjE3ODQyMjYxMzQsImV4cCI6MTc4NjgxODEzNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.2tIl_cHnk0XV41jfZr1DZPYtkg5__j2Cn-Vip447WmU)
### I'm honored to have the support of this civil rights icon.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Jul 16
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/jim-clyburns-endorsement-means-the?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA1NzY4MzA4LCJpYXQiOjE3ODQyMjYxMzQsImV4cCI6MTc4NjgxODEzNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.2tIl_cHnk0XV41jfZr1DZPYtkg5__j2Cn-Vip447WmU&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/jim-clyburns-endorsement-means-the?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Friends,
**I am honored to announce that Congressman Jim Clyburn is endorsing my campaign for the U.S. Senate in Michigan.**
It's been a privilege to work alongside him in the House for the past seven years.
Together, we have passed crucial legislation to help working families all over the country and stood up for what's right when Republicans have tried to drag our nation backward.
Folks, this is a man who knows what it takes to fight - and he knows what it takes to win.
To have his stamp of approval is deeply humbling and inspiring.
Since my first day in Congress, I've seen him model the kind of leadership that is rooted in service, creates meaningful change, and keeps community at the heart of everything.
That is what being a member of Congress is all about. Jim Clyburn is one of our nation's greatest examples of how to do it. He has the respect, admiration, and trust of his colleagues, his constituents, and Americans on both sides of the aisle because of it.
Jim Clyburn understands just how crucial keeping our state blue is right now.
He knows what we've been saying all along: The stakes are high in this battleground race. Senate control will very likely come down to Michigan. And the polls consistently show I'm the Democrat with the best chance at defeating Mike Rogers.
That's why Congressman Clyburn is jumping into this race.
**Because the truth is none of us can afford to pretend this is just another election - that no matter the outcome, everything will be fine in November. Losing this race isn't an option.**
This is a turning point. Costs are too high. Working families are struggling. And instead of helping lower costs for regular folks, Republicans are pandering to Trump and their MAGA billionaire donors - while doing their level best to strip away our basic rights and erode our democracy.
This is a five-alarm fire. Rep. Clyburn knows what it takes to meet this kind of moment because he's been putting in the work for years.
And to have his support sends a clear message to everyone watching - our opponents, pundits, and voters alike: This team has what it takes to win.
I am so grateful for this endorsement because it means that he believes in me and knows I can carry on the fight and meet the urgency of this moment with integrity, determination, and grit.
But more than that, I am grateful for his leadership. For his trust. For a chance to keep working alongside champions like him as we continue to fight for progress.
_And I 'm more fired up than ever to win._
But to do that, I'm going to need all the power of this entire team behind me.
[That's why I'm asking you to join Congressman Clyburn and lend your support to this campaign by chipping in any amount today. Every dollar gets us that much closer to winning in Michigan and flipping the Senate.](https://substack.com/redirect/b40dc79d-3f0a-4014-a4c0-4dcca9b1a36d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/b40dc79d-3f0a-4014-a4c0-4dcca9b1a36d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you so much for being with me in this fight.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/b40dc79d-3f0a-4014-a4c0-4dcca9b1a36d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

This week,
Supreme Court Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Elena Kagan showed up to
testify before Congress — the first time sitting justices have done so in
seven years.

But here’s the catch: they showed up to talk money, not accountability.

The Court is requesting a $20.6 million budget increase, part of it for
justices' security amid rising threats. Fair enough. But when it came to
ethics and transparency, the answers were much harder to come by:

They still won't commit to a real, enforceable ethics code.
They still hand down massive, life-altering rulings through the shadow
docket, with little to no explanation.
They still rule for billionaires, corporations, and the powerful, while
the rest of us live with the consequences.

And when pressed on ethics enforcement, Kagan called it an "open
question." Barrett said she's "less certain" it's even workable.^1

Translation: they'll discuss it forever. They just won't do it.

This is what unchecked power looks like. A Court that treats basic
accountability like it's optional and like the people don't deserve
answers. Enough is enough.

Demand Justice PAC exists to make sure the Court can't keep operating in
the dark. We’re demanding binding ethics rules, transparency on the shadow
docket, an expanded bench, and a Court that finally answers to the public.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260716.0pxdzy&refcode=em20260716-61636&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61636%2E1407376%2EwJZ6Yy ]The Court's arrogance isn't going to fix itself. Chip in
$5 to Demand Justice PAC right now and help us turn the
pressure up until accountability isn't optional anymore.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260716.0pxdzy&amount=5&refcode=em20260716-61636&t=1022&akid=61636%2E1407376%2EwJZ6Yy ]Donate $5 ››

In solidarity,

Team Demand Justice PAC

subject: The PA budget passed, but we need more

body:
| | | Peter, This weekend, Pennsylvania lawmakers passed a new state budget. But as people across the Commonwealth lose healthcare coverage and SNAP benefits because of massive federal cuts, it's clear Pennsylvania needs to do more. **In a year of brutal federal cuts, WFP and our allies at Tax Billionaires, Fund PA proposed real solutions to Pennsylvania’s affordability crisis.** The people who rely on SNAP and Medicaid spoke up, and legislators heard loud and clear that Pennsylvanians want the wealthiest billionaires and corporations in our state to pay their fair share so we can invest in the things our communities need. **One thing is clear: We need to increase revenue in Pennsylvania.** As deeper federal cuts take hold, our families will be hardest hit when the programs we rely on disappear. Next year’s budget _must_ include significant new revenue to fund what our families need, and the way to do it is by passing the revenue package we have proposed. **The package would corporate tax loopholes, tax big tech companies, and tax billionaires’ unearned income like Wall Street stock sales. This is commonsense policy that could fund healthcare, education, housing, or any other priorities that matter to the people of Pennsylvania.** [**Don't let lawmakers balance the budget on the backs of working families, Peter. clean_body: Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. Todd Blanche just said the quiet part out loud.
During his confirmation hearing to become Attorney General, he was asked about his relationship with Donald Trump.
**His response:_"I'm his lawyer." _**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135398812/634112655/789508428?refcode=260716_RG_toddblanche-lawyer&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNmEwM2ZlOC00ODgxLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5J8z--RT77mxzJTBzltIvQOMUfiPKKqvEyEVDJocelY=)
That wasn't just a slip of the tongue. It was a reminder of exactly why he's the wrong person to lead the Department of Justice.
The Attorney General isn't supposed to be the President's personal attorney. The Attorney General is supposed to represent the American people.
But Todd Blanche has spent months acting like his job is to protect one man: Donald Trump.
❌ He's been at the center of the administration's handling of the Epstein files.
❌ He's defended Trump's legal and political interests.
❌ And now Republicans want to reward that loyalty by putting him in charge of the entire Justice Department.
That's backward.
The Department of Justice should be independent. It should follow the facts — not political orders. And it should never be run by someone whose first instinct is to think of himself as the President's lawyer.
**That's why I've been clear from the beginning: Todd Blanche cannot be confirmed as Attorney General — he should be answering questions before the House Oversight Committee.**
**[The fight for transparency and accountability doesn't stop because Donald Trump wants another loyalist running the Justice Department. But we can’t keep up this work without your support. So I’m asking you personally to make a contribution today to help power our fight. name: David Hogg

body:
How we build campaigns from the ground up.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260716-1&t=1&akid=3733%2E587540%2EpK03Y2)
Peter,
When most people think about campaigns, they picture candidates giving speeches, knocking on doors, or debating on stage.
But that's only part of the story.
Behind every successful campaign is a team making phone calls late into the night, reviewing messaging, recruiting volunteers, raising money, building coalitions, and helping candidates navigate every challenge that comes with running for office.
**That's the work we're doing every single day at Leaders We Deserve.**
We don't just endorse young progressive candidates — **_we help build winning campaigns.**_
It starts with recruitment. We identify young leaders who have the potential to be the best representatives for their communities, especially the ones the political establishment too often overlooks.
Then we get to work.
We help campaigns build from the ground up by supporting them through their campaign launch, advising them on fundraising, recruiting staff, pitching their story to local and national news, advising them on messaging, coalition building, voter outreach, and volunteer recruitment. Our Campaigns Department works with our endorsed campaigns every day to ensure they are running the best operation and crafting the best strategy to win. On top of daily advising, we also run paid media campaigns to get our candidates’ message out to voters. Through grassroots support from people like you, we’re able to invest heavily and reach hundreds of thousands of voters in a district through mail campaigns, digital ads, and more.
It's not always glamorous.
Sometimes it means burning the midnight oil to review campaign plans before a big launch. Sometimes it's helping a first-time candidate prepare for an important interview or rushing to close a budget gap in order to keep a campaign ad on the air for one more week.
**But this is the work that wins elections.**
**[And it’s only possible because of grassroots donors like you. Can you make a $5 contribution today to ensure we can give our young, progressive candidates the support they need to win?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260716_1_supportcand.C02YAn&refcode=em20260716-3733&amount=5&t=2&akid=3733%2E587540%2EpK03Y2)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

body:
Important Information and Links

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/35fd60d36534/help-me-defeat-dan-crenshaw-18004638?e=8644c7c4ea)
---
| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
Friends,

What is the predicted hurricane season for 2026?
NOAA's outlook for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season, which runs **June 1 to November 30** , predicts a 35% chance of a near-normal season, a 10% chance of an above-normal season, and a 55% chance of a below-normal season. The agency is forecasting a total of 8-14 named storms (winds of 39 mph or higher).
Preparation is key! The below links can help you stay up to date during a storm.
---
|
---
| | **For the latest weather report**
---
| [Click for Weather Update](https://us.list-manage.com/qpPynkYLlk3?e=8644c7c4ea&c2id=9da2a6b80b05a64c75f009678d79cbb8)
---
| |
**Remember:** **"Turn Around, Don't Drown" — never drive through flooded roadways.****Check the latest road conditions and road closures.**
---
| [Road Updates](https://us.list-manage.com/p55RGDHU_Bh?e=8644c7c4ea&c2id=9da2a6b80b05a64c75f009678d79cbb8)
---
|
---

---
|

---

---
| [Centerpoint Outage Map](https://us.list-manage.com/XbSYnSpSTlO?e=8644c7c4ea&c2id=9da2a6b80b05a64c75f009678d79cbb8)
---
|
---
| |
Should you find yourself in an emergency situation and need help, easily find essential services and resources near you with the Montgomery County Aid Locator. This interactive application helps residents quickly locate shelters, food distribution centers, medical facilities, and other vital aid during emergencies and disasters.
---
| [Montgomery County Aid Locator]()
---
|
---
| |

Reminder - Important Hurricane Supplies:
* Bottled water: Storms can wreak havoc on water supplies, and drinkable water can be scarce in the days that follow a hurricane. Stock a 10-day supply of one gallon per person per day.

* First aid kit: Every home should have one with all the basics in one convenient carry-all.

* Ratcheting tie-downs: Secure outdoor items so they don’t become flying debris.

* Weather radio: Get weather alerts and emergency bulletins from the National Weather Service 24-hours a day.
* LED [flashlights](https://us.list-manage.com/L8tyX3FI0yi?e=8644c7c4ea&c2id=9da2a6b80b05a64c75f009678d79cbb8) and lanterns: Make sure you have one for every member of the family. Remember to have plenty of [extra batteries](https://us.list-manage.com/14X_J4vsjBW?e=8644c7c4ea&c2id=9da2a6b80b05a64c75f009678d79cbb8) to operate the flashlights.

* Generator: Have a portable generator or install a permanent generator for power outages. Follow safety instructions provided by the manufacturer. Make sure it’s running outside with the exhaust directed away from openings to your home or nearby buildings – at least 20-feet from any occupied buildings.

* CO alarm: Protect your family against any possible exposure to carbon monoxide fumes when using a portable generator.

* Tarp: Durable tarps with weather-resistant polyethylene coating in large sizes are great for covering roof damage.

* Power inverters: In the event of electrical failure, you can power small items in your home from your car with this non-interruptible backup power source.

* Extension cords: These are essential for helping provide power from generators to items you need to run.

* Gas cans: Don’t run out of gas. Keep an emergency supply safely on hand for your generators and chain saws.

body:
Republicans passed Trump’s big ugly budget bill a year ago this month.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3556%2E21716%2EcdR1GP)
**Republicans passed Trump’s big ugly budget bill a year ago this month.** I’m sad to say that since then, the effects of the bill have been just as bad as Democrats said they would be.
Recently, I wrote an op-ed for the _Cape Gazette_ to shine a light on the devastating impact this legislation is having on our neighbors in Sussex County and across Delaware.
I hope you’ll take a few minutes to read my op-ed and help me continue sounding the alarm. The more people learn about MAGA’s cruelty and deceit, the harder it’ll be for them to get away with it.
— Sarah
* * *
Care in Sussex County needs investment, not cuts
_Sarah McBride_
_July 7, 2026_
This month marks one year since the passage of President Trump’s so-called “One Big Beautiful Bill” Act, which pushed healthcare out of reach for millions of Americans through the single largest cut to the American healthcare system in history. Across the country, fewer people have health insurance, hospitals and clinics are shutting down, and there’s growing concern about access to care, especially in rural communities. For my neighbors across Sussex County, access to quality, affordable healthcare is about more than convenience – it's about the security and dignity that come from knowing the care you need will be there when you need it.
Sussex County is the fastest-growing region of our state. It is also home to a growing population of retirees and older adults. Together, this combination places enormous pressure on an already strained healthcare system. Providers in Sussex County are working tirelessly to meet the demand, all while facing workforce shortages, financial strain and a system that fails to account for the distinct needs of rural communities. For many families, whether based in western or eastern Sussex County, seeing a specialist already means driving long distances and spending more on gas just to get the care they need. When care is delayed or providers disappear, those distances become yet another barrier to staying healthy.
Rural providers were already struggling to keep hospitals open, recruit doctors and nurses, and meet growing demand, and now, they’re being asked to do even more with fewer resources. At a moment when rural healthcare should have been strengthened, President Trump and congressional Republicans chose to do the opposite: they raided Americans’ healthcare – all to give tax breaks to their billionaire friends while working people in Delaware pay the price.
Trump and congressional Republicans’ “Big Beautiful Bill” aims to cut as much as $4 billion in federal Medicaid funding to Delaware over the next decade. More than 30,000 Delawareans are projected to lose their Medicaid coverage, Marketplace enrollment in Delaware has already declined by 16%, and more than 18,000 of our neighbors have lost food assistance because of this heartless law. These aren’t just numbers – they are our parents, grandparents, coworkers, friends and neighbors, all seeking the same thing: the chance to stay healthy, care for their families and age with dignity.
Here in Sussex County, where providers are already working to keep pace with rapid growth and an aging population, residents are feeling the weight of cuts to Medicaid and federal healthcare funding. They show up here at home – with longer wait times, fewer providers accepting patients, higher healthcare costs for all of us, and more strain on the hospitals and clinics our communities rely on.
Roughly 42% of births in Delaware are covered by Medicaid, yet access to OB-GYN providers remains limited. This lack of infrastructure forces many expecting parents to travel outside the county to give birth. The same is true for specialty care. Patients recovering from cancer treatment or organ transplants often require consistent follow-up appointments, yet many are forced to travel to Wilmington or even outside Delaware to receive care.
And mental healthcare remains another pressing need. Sussex County continues to face a federally recognized shortage of behavioral health and psychiatric providers. This means families seeking support for anxiety, depression, substance-use disorders or other mental health challenges are saddled with long waits and limited provider availability.
We know what works: investing in rural hospitals, supporting our federally qualified health centers, strengthening the healthcare workforce, protecting Medicaid, expanding access to mental healthcare, and ensuring that where you live never determines whether you can get the care you need. We must never accept a status quo where ZIP codes serve as barriers to treatment.
No family should have to cross county lines to welcome a child into the world. No cancer patient should have to spend hours on the road for reliable, lifesaving care. And no one seeking mental healthcare should be forced to wait months for treatment. That is the future Sussex County deserves.

More than 30,000 Delawareans are projected to lose their Medicaid coverage, Marketplace enrollment in Delaware has already declined by 16%, and more than 18,000 of our neighbors have lost food assistance because of this heartless law. These aren’t just numbers – they are our parents, grandparents, coworkers, friends and neighbors, all seeking the same thing: the chance to stay healthy, care for their families and age with dignity. Here in Sussex County, where providers are already working to keep pace with rapid growth and an aging population, residents are feeling the weight of cuts to Medicaid and federal healthcare funding. They show up here at home – with longer wait times, fewer providers accepting patients, higher healthcare costs for all of us, and more strain on the hospitals and clinics our communities rely on. Roughly 42% of births in Delaware are covered by Medicaid, yet access to OB-GYN providers remains limited. This lack of infrastructure forces many expecting parents to travel outside the county to give birth. The same is true for specialty care. Patients recovering from cancer treatment or organ transplants often require consistent follow-up appointments, yet many are forced to travel to Wilmington or even outside Delaware to receive care. And mental healthcare remains another pressing need. Sussex County continues to face a federally recognized shortage of behavioral health and psychiatric providers. This means families seeking support for anxiety, depression, substance-use disorders or other mental health challenges are saddled with long waits and limited provider availability. We know what works: investing in rural hospitals, supporting our federally qualified health centers, strengthening the healthcare workforce, protecting Medicaid, expanding access to mental healthcare, and ensuring that where you live never determines whether you can get the care you need. We must never accept a status quo where ZIP codes serve as barriers to treatment. No family should have to cross county lines to welcome a child into the world. No cancer patient should have to spend hours on the road for reliable, lifesaving care. And no one seeking mental healthcare should be forced to wait months for treatment. That is the future Sussex County deserves. Thank you for reading! Sarah is working every day to push back against Trump’s billionaire agenda, hold Republicans accountable for the harm they’re causing, and deliver real solutions to make life more affordable for working families. None of that is possible without this grassroots team.

LAST CALL: Sign the pledge to support a brighter future for working Texans
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Hear%20America.png]
These last few weeks, TOP has teamed up with our friends at the Organizing Revival Network to promote the Willing to Fight Pledge [https://toptx.us/orn] -- a commitment to a vision and future where ALL Texans have the ability to grow and thrive.
We're only a few days from our end-of-June deadline. Can you sign the pledge today to help us reach our completed pledge goal? [https://toptx.us/orn]
It only takes a minute and your feedback provides our groups with a look at what issues matter most to you and your family.
👉🏾 Take the pledge now! [https://toptx.us/orn]
Celebrating our communities and building fellowship this Juneteenth
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/01%202026%20Juneteenth.jpg]
TOP staff and members celebrated Juneteenth alongside community partners at events across Houston, Dallas, and San Antonio this past week. Through that celebration we honor the ancestors we stand on the shoulders of, and recommit to working tirelessly toward a future where race and class are no longer barriers to justice and opportunity in our country.
Juneteenth serves as a renewed call to unite against racial and economic injustice, so that we can chart a path toward a stronger Texas and nation that uplifts and empowers every Black person, regardless of their background or economic status. This is why we organize. This is why we are stronger together.
Taking time this summer to refuel for the second half of 2026
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/TOP%20summer%202026%20out.jpg]
TOP offices will be closed Saturday, June 27 - Sunday, July 5, as we take time to rest, rejuvenate, and prepare for a busy rest of 2026 filled with organizing and getting out the vote! You can still keep in touch with us online, though. Give us a follow on the following platforms:
Facebook [https://www.facebook.com/texasorganizingproject/]
Instagram [https://www.instagram.com/texasorganizingproject]
BlackTOP Instagram [https://www.instagram.com/blacktoptexas]
TikTok [https://www.tiktok.com/@organizetexas]
X (Twitter) [https://x.com/TXOrgProject]
Bluesky [https://bsky.app/profile/txorgproject.bsky.social]

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Summer%202026%20vacation%20photo%20tips.jpg]
Taking quality phone pics can be easier said than done! Whether you're traveling abroad, across the state, or just within your community this summer, utilize these easy tips [https://www.techadvisor.com/article/3170604/8-professional-tips-for-better-smartphone-photos.html] on how to get the most out of your smartphone photos this summer to capture those special moments.

ÚLTIMA OPORTUNIDAD: Firma el compromiso para apoyar un futuro mejor para los trabajadores de Texas
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Hear%20America.png]
En las últimas semanas, TOP se ha unido a nuestros amigos de Organizing Revival Network para promover el compromiso "Willing to Fight" [https://toptx.us/orn] (Dispuestos a Luchar): un compromiso con una visión y un futuro en los que TODOS los tejanos tengan la oportunidad de crecer y prosperar.

Solo te llevará un minuto, y tu opinión nos permitirá saber qué temas son los más importantes para ti y tu familia.
👉🏾 ¡Firma el compromiso ahora! [https://toptx.us/orn]
Celebrando a nuestras comunidades y fortaleciendo la camaradería en este Juneteenth
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/01%202026%20Juneteenth.jpg]
La semana pasada, el personal y los miembros de TOP celebraron Juneteenth junto a aliados comunitarios en eventos realizados en Houston, Dallas y San Antonio. A través de esta celebración, honramos a los ancestros sobre cuyos hombros nos apoyamos y reafirmamos nuestro compromiso de trabajar incansablemente por un futuro en el que la raza y la clase social ya no sean barreras para la justicia y las oportunidades en nuestro país.
Juneteenth representa un llamado renovado a unirnos contra la injusticia racial y económica, para así trazar el camino hacia un Texas y una nación más fuertes que impulsen y empoderen a cada persona afrodescendiente, independientemente de sus antecedentes o situación económica. We're only a few days from our end-of-June deadline. Can you sign the pledge today to help us reach our completed pledge goal? [] It only takes a minute and your feedback provides our groups with a look at what issues matter most to you and your family. 👉🏾 Take the pledge now! Through that celebration we honor the ancestors we stand on the shoulders of, and recommit to working tirelessly toward a future where race and class are no longer barriers to justice and opportunity in our country. Juneteenth serves as a renewed call to unite against racial and economic injustice, so that we can chart a path toward a stronger Texas and nation that uplifts and empowers every Black person, regardless of their background or economic status. This is why we organize. This is why we are stronger together.
